title.zh: 卷一百二十六 列傳第十四 李文忠 鄧愈 湯和 沐英
title.en: Volume 126 Biographies 14: Li Wenzhong, Deng Yu, Tang He, Mu Ying
title.raw: 卷一百二十六 列傳第十四 李文忠 鄧愈 湯和 沐英 Volume 126 Biographies 14: Li Wenzhong, Deng Yu, Tang He, Mu Ying

sentences.zh: 李文忠

translations.literal: Li Wenzhong
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenzhong

sentences.zh: 李文忠，字思本，小字保兒，盱眙人，太祖姊子也。

translations.literal: Li Wenzhong, courtesy name Siben, childhood name Bao'er, was a native of Xuyi and a nephew of the Founder, being the son of his elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenzhong, whose courtesy name was Siben and childhood name Bao'er, came from Xuyi. He was the Founder's nephew, born to the Founder's elder sister.

sentences.zh: 年十二而母死，父貞攜之轉側亂軍中，瀕死者數矣。

translations.literal: When he was twelve his mother died; his father Zhen carried him through the turmoil of contending armies, and several times he came near death.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died when he was twelve. His father Li Zhen led him from camp to camp through the chaos of war, and more than once the boy nearly lost his life.

sentences.zh: 逾二年乃謁太祖于滁陽。

translations.literal: After more than two years he finally had an audience with the Founder at Chuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Only after two more years did he finally reach Chuyang and present himself to the Founder.

sentences.zh: 太祖見保兒，喜甚，撫以為子，令從己姓。

translations.literal: When the Founder saw Bao'er he was greatly pleased, caressed him and made him his son, and ordered him to take the Founder's surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was overjoyed to see Bao'er. He took the boy in as his own son and had him adopt the Zhu surname.

sentences.zh: 讀書穎敏如素習。

translations.literal: In reading he was sharp and quick, as though he had long practiced it.
translations.idiomatic: In his studies he proved quick and perceptive, as if he had been at his books all his life.

sentences.zh: 年十九，以舍人將親軍，從援池州，破天完軍，驍勇冠諸將。

translations.literal: At nineteen, as an attendant he commanded the personal guard; he followed the army to relieve Chizhou, routed the Tianwan forces, and in fierce valor ranked first among the generals.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he led the personal guard as an imperial attendant. On the relief march to Chizhou he shattered the Tianwan army, and none among the generals matched his daring in battle.

sentences.zh: 別攻青陽、石埭、太平、旌德，皆下之。

translations.literal: On separate campaigns he attacked Qingyang, Shidi, Taiping, and Jingde, and took them all.
translations.idiomatic: He then led separate attacks on Qingyang, Shidi, Taiping, and Jingde, capturing every one of them.

sentences.zh: 敗元院判阿魯灰於萬年街，復敗苗軍于於潛、昌化。

translations.literal: He defeated the Yuan vice-censor Aru Hui at Wannian Street, and again defeated the Miao armies at Yuqian and Changhua.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the Yuan vice-censor Aru Hui at Wannian Street, then beat the Miao forces again at Yuqian and Changhua.

sentences.zh: 進攻淳安，夜襲洪元帥，降其眾千餘，授帳前左副都指揮兼領元帥府事。

translations.literal: Advancing against Chun'an, he raided Marshal Hong by night, accepted the surrender of more than a thousand of his men, and was appointed Left Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard and concurrently placed in charge of the Marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Chun'an he struck Marshal Hong's camp by night, took the surrender of more than a thousand troops, and was made Left Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard with concurrent charge of the Marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尋會鄧愈、胡大海之師，取建德，以為嚴州府，守之。

translations.literal: Soon he joined the armies of Deng Yu and Hu Dahai, took Jiande, made it the prefecture of Yanzhou, and garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: He soon united with the forces of Deng Yu and Hu Dahai, seized Jiande, established it as Yanzhou Prefecture, and remained to defend it.

sentences.zh: 苗帥楊完者以苗、僚數萬水陸奄至。

translations.literal: The Miao commander Yang Wanzhe brought several tens of thousands of Miao and Liao troops by land and water and suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao commander Yang Wanzhe swept in by land and water with tens of thousands of Miao and Liao troops.

sentences.zh: 文忠將輕兵破其陸軍，取所馘首，浮巨筏上。

translations.literal: Wenzhong led light troops to break their land army, took the severed heads they had cut off, and floated them on great rafts.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong led light infantry against their land force, collected the severed heads, and set them adrift on great rafts.

sentences.zh: 水軍見之亦遁。

translations.literal: When the naval force saw this they too fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy fleet saw the heads, it fled as well.

sentences.zh: 完者復來犯，與鄧愈擊卻之。

translations.literal: Wanzhe came to attack again; together with Deng Yu, Wenzhong beat him back.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanzhe attacked again, Wenzhong and Deng Yu drove him off.

sentences.zh: 進克浦江，禁焚掠，示恩信。

translations.literal: Advancing, he took Pujiang, forbade burning and plunder, and showed favor and good faith.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and captured Pujiang, forbidding looting and burning while making a show of mercy and trustworthiness.

sentences.zh: 義門鄭氏避兵山谷，招之還，以兵護之。

translations.literal: The Zheng clan of the Righteous Gate had fled the armies into the mountains and valleys; he summoned them back and protected them with troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Zheng clan of the famed Righteous Gate had taken refuge in the hills; he called them home and posted troops to guard them.

sentences.zh: 民大悅。

translations.literal: The people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The populace rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 完者死，其部將乞降，撫之，得三萬餘人。

translations.literal: When Wanzhe died, his subordinate generals begged to surrender; he pacified them and gained more than thirty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: After Wanzhe's death his officers sought surrender. Wenzhong won them over and absorbed more than thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 與胡大海拔諸暨。

translations.literal: Together with Hu Dahai he took Zhuji.
translations.idiomatic: He and Hu Dahai captured Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 張士誠寇嚴州，禦之東門，使別將出小北門，間道襲其後，夾擊大破之。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng raided Yanzhou; Wenzhong met him at the east gate, sent another general out through the small north gate to strike his rear by a hidden path, and with a pincer attack inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shicheng attacked Yanzhou, Wenzhong held the east gate while sending another commander through the lesser north gate to hit the enemy's rear by a side road. The double assault routed Zhang's army.

sentences.zh: 逾月，復來攻，又破之大浪灘，乘勝克分水。

translations.literal: After more than a month they came to attack again; he again defeated them at Dalangtan and, pressing the victory, took Fenshui.
translations.idiomatic: A month later the enemy returned; he beat them again at Dalangtan and, riding the momentum, seized Fenshui.

sentences.zh: 士誠遣將據三溪，復擊敗之，斬陸元帥，焚其壘。

translations.literal: Shicheng sent generals to hold Sanxi; Wenzhong again defeated them, beheaded Marshal Lu, and burned their camps.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng sent troops to hold Sanxi, but Wenzhong defeated them once more, slew Marshal Lu, and burned their fortifications.

sentences.zh: 士誠自是不敢窺嚴州。

translations.literal: Shicheng himself no longer dared cast his eyes toward Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After that Shicheng himself never again dared threaten Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 進同僉行樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Associate Censor-in-Chief of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Associate Censor-in-Chief of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 胡大海得漢將李明道、王漢二，送文忠所，釋而禮之，使招建昌守將王溥。

translations.literal: Hu Dahai captured the Han generals Li Mingdao and Wang Han and sent them to Wenzhong's headquarters; Wenzhong released them and treated them with courtesy, and had them summon Wang Pu, the defending general of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Dahai captured the Han generals Li Mingdao and Wang Han and sent them to Wenzhong, who freed them and received them honorably, then sent them to persuade Wang Pu, the Jianchang garrison commander, to surrender.

sentences.zh: 溥降。

translations.literal: Pu surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu submitted.

sentences.zh: 苗將蔣英、劉震殺大海，以金華叛。

translations.literal: The Miao generals Jiang Ying and Liu Zhen killed Dahai and rebelled with Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao generals Jiang Ying and Liu Zhen murdered Hu Dahai and rose in revolt from Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 文忠遣將擊走之，親撫定其眾。

translations.literal: Wenzhong sent generals to strike and drive them off, and personally went to pacify and settle their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong sent officers to drive them off, then went in person to calm and reorganize the troops.

sentences.zh: 處州苗軍亦殺耿再成叛。

translations.literal: The Miao army of Chuzhou also killed Geng Zaicheng and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao forces in Chuzhou likewise killed Geng Zaicheng and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 文忠遣將屯縉雲以圖之。

translations.literal: Wenzhong sent generals to encamp at Jinyun in order to plan against them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong posted troops at Jinyun to prepare an operation against them.

sentences.zh: 拜浙東行省左丞，總制嚴、衢、信、處、諸全軍事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Vice Minister of the Zhejiang Eastern Branch Secretariat and given overall command of military affairs in Yan, Qu, Xin, Chu, and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Left Vice Minister of the Zhejiang Eastern Branch Secretariat with overall command of the armies of Yan, Qu, Xin, Chu, and Zhu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 吳兵十萬方急攻諸全，守將謝再興告急，遣同僉胡德濟往援。

translations.literal: A hundred thousand Wu troops were pressing the attack on Zhu; the defending general Xie Zaixing reported an emergency, and Wenzhong sent Associate Censor Hu Deji to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand Wu troops were fiercely besieging Zhu when the defender Xie Zaixing sent an urgent appeal for help. Wenzhong dispatched Associate Censor Hu Deji to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 再興復請益兵，文忠兵少無以應。

translations.literal: Zaixing again asked for more troops, but Wenzhong's forces were few and he had none to send.
translations.idiomatic: Zaixing asked again for reinforcements, but Wenzhong had too few men to spare any.

sentences.zh: 會太祖使邵榮討處州亂卒，文忠乃揚言徐右丞、邵平章將大軍刻日進。

translations.literal: It happened that the Founder had sent Shao Rong to suppress the mutinous troops of Chuzhou; Wenzhong then spread word that Vice Minister Xu and Pacification Commissioner Shao would advance with a great army on a set day.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Founder sent Shao Rong against the Chuzhou mutineers, and Wenzhong spread the rumor that Vice Minister Xu and Pacification Commissioner Shao were marching with a great host and would arrive within days.

sentences.zh: 吳軍聞之懼，謀夜遁。

translations.literal: When the Wu army heard this they were afraid and planned to flee by night.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu troops took fright at the report and plotted a night withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 德濟與再興帥死士夜半開門突擊，大破之，諸全遂完。

translations.literal: Deji and Zaixing led death-defying warriors, opened the gates at midnight, and made a sudden assault, inflicting a great defeat, and Zhu was thus preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Deji and Zaixing led picked men in a midnight sortie through the gates and shattered the enemy, saving Zhu from capture.

sentences.zh: 明年，再興叛降于吳，以吳軍犯東陽。

translations.literal: The next year Zaixing rebelled and surrendered to Wu, and with Wu troops invaded Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zaixing defected to Wu and led Wu forces against Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 文忠與胡深迎戰于義烏，將千騎橫突其陣，大敗之。

translations.literal: Wenzhong and Hu Shen met them in battle at Yiwu; leading a thousand horsemen he charged straight through their battle line and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong and Hu Shen met them at Yiwu. At the head of a thousand horsemen he drove straight through their line and routed them.

sentences.zh: 已，用深策去諸全五十里別築一城，以相掎角。

translations.literal: Afterward, adopting Shen's plan, he built another city fifty li from Zhu so that the two could support each other like pincers.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Shen's advice and built a second walled town fifty li from Zhu so the two posts could shield each other.

sentences.zh: 士誠遣司徒李伯升以十六萬眾來攻，不克。

translations.literal: Shicheng sent the Minister of Works Li Bosheng with a hundred and sixty thousand men to attack, but they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng sent Minister of Works Li Bosheng with a hundred and sixty thousand men against the new town, but they failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復以二十萬眾攻新城。

translations.literal: After more than a year they came again with two hundred thousand men to attack the new city.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later they returned with two hundred thousand men to assault the new town.

sentences.zh: 文忠帥硃亮祖等馳救，去新城十里而軍。

translations.literal: Wenzhong led Zhu Liangzu and others in a rapid relief march and encamped ten li from the new city.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong hurried to the rescue at the head of Zhu Liangzu and others, halting his army ten li from the new town.

sentences.zh: 德濟使人告賊勢盛，宜少駐以俟大軍。

translations.literal: Deji sent a messenger saying the enemy's strength was great and that they ought to halt briefly and wait for the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Deji sent word that the enemy was too strong and urged Wenzhong to hold back until the main force arrived.

sentences.zh: 文忠曰：「兵在謀不在眾。」

translations.literal: Wenzhong said: "In warfare what matters is stratagem, not numbers."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong replied, "Victory depends on strategy, not numbers."

sentences.zh: 乃下令曰：「彼眾而驕，我少而銳，以銳遇驕，必克之矣。

translations.literal: He then issued an order, saying: "They are many but arrogant; we are few but keen. When the keen meet the arrogant, we are sure to overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: He then proclaimed to his men, "They are numerous but arrogant; we are few but fierce. Fierce troops meeting arrogant ones will surely prevail.

sentences.zh: 彼軍輜重山積，此天以富汝曹也。

translations.literal: Their army's baggage and supplies are heaped like mountains; Heaven is using this to enrich you all.
translations.idiomatic: Their wagons and supplies are piled like hills—Heaven means to make you rich today.

sentences.zh: 勉之。」

translations.literal: Strive on."
translations.idiomatic: Do your utmost."

sentences.zh: 會有白氣自東北來覆軍上，占之曰「必勝」。

translations.literal: Just then a white vapor came from the northeast and spread over the army; divination of it was pronounced "certain victory."
translations.idiomatic: At that moment a white mist rolled in from the northeast and shrouded the army; the diviners declared it a sign of certain victory.

sentences.zh: 詰朝會戰，天大霧晦冥，文忠集諸將仰天誓曰：「國家之事在此一舉，文忠不敢愛死以後三軍。」

translations.literal: At dawn they joined battle; the sky was thick with fog and darkness. Wenzhong gathered the generals, looked up to Heaven, and swore: "The fate of the state hangs on this single stroke; Wenzhong dares not spare his life and leave the three armies behind."
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they joined battle in pitch fog. Wenzhong assembled his officers, looked to Heaven, and swore: "The fate of the realm rests on this day. I will not hold back my life and leave the army leaderless."

sentences.zh: 乃使元帥徐大興、湯克明等將左軍，嚴德、王德等將右軍，而自以中軍當敵沖。

translations.literal: He then had the marshals Xu Daxing, Tang Keming, and others command the left wing; Yan De, Wang De, and others the right wing; and himself took the center to meet the enemy's main thrust.
translations.idiomatic: He placed Xu Daxing, Tang Keming, and others in command of the left wing, Yan De and Wang De of the right, and himself took the center against the enemy's main thrust.

sentences.zh: 會處州援兵亦至，奮前搏擊。

translations.literal: Just then the relief troops from Chuzhou also arrived and pressed forward to grapple in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou reinforcements arrived at the same moment and threw themselves into the fight.

sentences.zh: 霧稍開，文忠橫槊引鐵騎數十，乘高馳下，沖其中堅。

translations.literal: As the fog lifted slightly, Wenzhong levelled his spear, led several tens of armored horsemen, charged down from the heights, and struck their center.
translations.idiomatic: As the fog thinned, Wenzhong levelled his spear, led a few dozen armored horsemen down from the heights, and drove into the enemy center.

sentences.zh: 敵以精騎圍文忠數重。

translations.literal: The enemy surrounded Wenzhong with elite cavalry in several rings.
translations.idiomatic: Elite enemy horsemen surrounded Wenzhong in ring after ring.

sentences.zh: 文忠手所格殺甚眾，縱騎馳突，所向皆披靡。

translations.literal: With his own hand he cut down a great many in close combat; he let his horsemen charge and thrust, and wherever they went all were swept aside.
translations.idiomatic: He killed many with his own blade, then spurred his riders forward; wherever they charged the enemy lines broke apart.

sentences.zh: 大軍乘之，城中兵亦鼓噪出，敵遂大潰。

translations.literal: The main army pressed the advantage; the troops in the city also beat drums and shouted as they sallied forth, and the enemy then fled in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: The main force pressed the attack while the garrison poured out with a great clamor, and the enemy collapsed in full rout.

sentences.zh: 逐北數十里，斬首數萬級，溪水盡赤，獲將校六百，甲士三千，鎧仗芻粟收數日不盡，伯升僅以身免。

translations.literal: They pursued the fleeing enemy for several tens of li, cut off tens of thousands of heads until the streams ran red, captured six hundred officers and men, three thousand armored soldiers, and armor, weapons, fodder, and grain that could not be gathered up in several days; Bosheng alone escaped with his body.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran for miles. Tens of thousands were beheaded until the streams ran red. Six hundred officers, three thousand armored soldiers, and mountains of arms, armor, fodder, and grain fell into their hands—loot enough to keep men gathering for days. Bosheng alone escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，太祖大喜，召歸，宴勞彌日，賜禦衣名馬，遣還鎮。

translations.literal: When news of the victory arrived the Founder was greatly pleased; he summoned Wenzhong back, feasted and rewarded him for days on end, bestowed imperial robes and famous horses, and sent him back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: When word of the victory reached the Founder he was overjoyed. He recalled Wenzhong, feasted him for days, gave him imperial robes and fine horses, and sent him back to his post.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，大軍伐吳，令攻杭州以牽制之。

translations.literal: The next autumn the main army campaigned against Wu and ordered him to attack Hangzhou in order to pin down the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn, as the main army marched against Wu, he was ordered to strike Hangzhou and tie down the enemy's forces.

sentences.zh: 文忠帥亮祖等克桐廬、新城、富陽，遂攻余杭。

translations.literal: Wenzhong led Liangzu and others to take Tonglu, Xincheng, and Fuyang, then attacked Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong led Liangzu and the others in capturing Tonglu, Xincheng, and Fuyang, then moved against Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 守將謝五，再興弟也，諭之降，許以不死。

translations.literal: The defending general Xie Wu was Zaixing's younger brother; Wenzhong urged him to surrender and promised he would not be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: The defender Xie Wu was Zaixing's younger brother. Wenzhong persuaded him to surrender and promised his life.

sentences.zh: 五與再興子五人出降。

translations.literal: Wu came out to surrender together with Zaixing's five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Wu came out with Zaixing's five sons to submit.

sentences.zh: 諸將請僇之，文忠不可。

translations.literal: The generals asked to execute them, but Wenzhong would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals demanded their execution, but Wenzhong refused.

sentences.zh: 遂趨杭州，守將潘元明亦降，整軍入。

translations.literal: He then pressed on to Hangzhou; the defending general Pan Yuanming also surrendered, and he entered the city with his army in good order.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to Hangzhou, where Pan Yuanming also surrendered, and Wenzhong led his troops into the city in good order.

sentences.zh: 元明以女樂迎，麾去之。

translations.literal: Yuanming welcomed him with female musicians; he waved them away.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanming tried to greet him with singing girls and musicians; Wenzhong waved them away.

sentences.zh: 營於麗譙，下令曰：「擅入民居者死。」

translations.literal: He encamped at the ceremonial tower and issued an order: "Anyone who enters private dwellings without authorization shall die."
translations.idiomatic: He pitched camp at the ceremonial gate tower and proclaimed, "Anyone who enters a private home without leave dies."

sentences.zh: 一卒借民釜，斬以徇，城中帖然。

translations.literal: One soldier borrowed a commoner's cooking pot and was beheaded as an example; the city became thoroughly calm.
translations.idiomatic: When one soldier borrowed a cooking pot from a household, Wenzhong had him beheaded as an example, and the city fell utterly quiet.

sentences.zh: 得兵三萬，糧二十萬。

translations.literal: He obtained thirty thousand troops and two hundred thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He gained thirty thousand soldiers and two hundred thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 就加榮祿大夫、浙江行省平章事，復姓李氏。

translations.literal: He was thereupon additionally appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Pacification Commissioner of the Zhejiang Branch Secretariat, and his original surname Li was restored.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted on the spot to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Pacification Commissioner of Zhejiang, and his surname was restored to Li.

sentences.zh: 大軍征閩，文忠別引軍屯浦城以逼之。

translations.literal: When the main army campaigned against Fujian, Wenzhong led a separate force to encamp at Pucheng in order to press upon it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Fujian campaign he led a separate force to garrison Pucheng and pressure the enemy.

sentences.zh: 師還，余寇金子隆等聚眾剽掠，文忠復討擒之，遂定建、延、汀三州。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the remaining bandits Jin Zilong and others gathered crowds to plunder; Wenzhong again campaigned, captured them, and thus settled the three prefectures of Jian, Yan, and Ting.
translations.idiomatic: After the army withdrew, remnant raiders led by Jin Zilong banded together to plunder. Wenzhong campaigned again, captured them, and secured Jian, Yan, and Ting prefectures.

sentences.zh: 命軍中收養道上棄兒，所全活無算。

translations.literal: He ordered the army to take in abandoned children along the roads; the number thus saved cannot be reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his troops to take in infants abandoned along the roads, saving untold lives.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年春，以偏將軍從右副將軍常遇春出塞，薄上都，走元帝，語具《遇春傳》。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Hongwu, as Vice General he followed the Right Vice General Chang Yuchun beyond the passes, pressed close to Shangdu, and drove off the Yuan emperor—the account is given in full in the Biography of Chang Yuchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Hongwu 2 he served as vice general under the Right Vice General Chang Yuchun on a campaign beyond the frontier that pressed Shangdu and drove off the Yuan emperor; the full account appears in Chang Yuchun's biography.

sentences.zh: 遇春卒，命文忠代將其軍，奉詔會大將軍徐達攻慶陽。

translations.literal: When Yuchun died, Wenzhong was ordered to take command of his army in his stead and, by imperial command, joined the Great General Xu Da in attacking Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuchun's death Wenzhong was placed in command of his army and ordered to join the Great General Xu Da in the assault on Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 行次太原，聞大同圍急，謂左丞趙庸曰：「我等受命而來，閫外之事苟利於國，專之可也。

translations.literal: Marching, they halted at Taiyuan; hearing that the siege of Datong was urgent, he said to the Left Vice Minister Zhao Yong: "We have received our commission and come forth; in matters outside the commander's seal, if they benefit the state, we may act on our own authority.
translations.idiomatic: On the march they stopped at Taiyuan. Hearing that Datong was in desperate straits, he told the Left Vice Minister Zhao Yong, "We were sent on imperial commission. Where affairs beyond the capital serve the state, we may act on our own authority.

sentences.zh: 今大同甚急，援之便。」

translations.literal: Now Datong is in great urgency; it is fitting to relieve it."
translations.idiomatic: Datong is in grave peril now—relief is the right move."

sentences.zh: 遂出雁門，次馬邑，敗元遊兵，擒平章劉帖木，進至白楊門。

translations.literal: He then went out through Yanmen, halted at Mayi, defeated Yuan scouting troops, captured the Pacification Commissioner Liu Tiemuer, and advanced to Baiyangmen.
translations.idiomatic: He marched out through Yanmen Pass, halted at Mayi, routed Yuan scouts, captured Pacification Commissioner Liu Tiemuer, and advanced to Baiyangmen.

sentences.zh: 天雨雪，已駐營，文忠令移前五里，阻水自固。

translations.literal: Heaven sent rain and snow; they had already encamped when Wenzhong ordered a move forward five li to block the water and secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Snow and rain fell as they camped. Wenzhong ordered the army forward five li to a position backed by water where they could stand firm.

sentences.zh: 元兵乘夜來劫，文忠堅壁不動。

translations.literal: Yuan troops came to raid by night; Wenzhong held fast within his walls and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan forces raided by night, but Wenzhong held his lines and did not stir.

sentences.zh: 質明，敵大至。

translations.literal: At first light the enemy arrived in force.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the enemy came in full strength.

sentences.zh: 以二營委之，殊死戰，度敵疲，乃出精兵左右擊，大破之，擒其將脫列伯，俘斬萬餘人，窮追至莽哥倉而還。

translations.literal: He committed two camps to them and fought to the death; estimating that the enemy was weary, he then sent out elite troops to strike from left and right, inflicted a great defeat, captured their general Tuoleibo, took and slew more than ten thousand men, and pursued to the limit at Manggecang before returning.
translations.idiomatic: He threw two camps into a desperate holding fight, then, judging the enemy spent, sent elite troops to strike from both flanks. The Yuan army was shattered. He captured the general Tuoleibo, killed or took more than ten thousand men, and pursued as far as Manggecang before turning back.

sentences.zh: 明年拜征虜左副將軍。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Left Vice General of the Pacification Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was named Left Vice General of the Pacification Campaign.

sentences.zh: 與大將軍分道北征，以十萬人出野狐嶺，至興和，降其守將。

translations.literal: He and the Great General marched north on separate routes; with a hundred thousand men he went out through Wild Fox Ridge, reached Xinghe, and accepted the surrender of its defending general.
translations.idiomatic: He and the Great General marched north by separate routes. With a hundred thousand men he crossed Wild Fox Ridge, reached Xinghe, and accepted the surrender of its garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 進兵察罕腦兒，擒平章竹真。

translations.literal: Advancing to Chahan Nur, he captured the Pacification Commissioner Zhuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Chahan Nur and captured Pacification Commissioner Zhuzhen.

sentences.zh: 次駱駝山，走平章沙不丁。

translations.literal: Halting at Camel Mountain, he drove off the Pacification Commissioner Shabuding.
translations.idiomatic: At Camel Mountain he put Pacification Commissioner Shabuding to flight.

sentences.zh: 次開平，降平章上都罕等。

translations.literal: Halting at Kaiping, he accepted the surrender of the Pacification Commissioner Shangduhan and others.
translations.idiomatic: At Kaiping he received the surrender of Pacification Commissioner Shangduhan and others.

sentences.zh: 時元帝已崩，太子愛猷識裏達臘新立。

translations.literal: At that time the Yuan emperor had already died and the crown prince Ayushiridara had newly been enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Yuan emperor was dead and the crown prince Ayushiridara had just ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 文忠諜知之，兼程趨應昌。

translations.literal: Wenzhong learned this through spies and, doubling his stages, hurried toward Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong learned this through his spies and forced the march to Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 元嗣君北走，獲其嫡子買的立八剌暨後妃宮人諸王將相官屬數百人，及宋、元玉璽金寶十五，玉冊二，鎮圭、大圭、玉帶、玉斧各一。

translations.literal: The Yuan successor fled north; Wenzhong captured his legitimate son Buyandalba together with several hundred consorts, palace women, princes, generals, ministers, and officials, as well as fifteen jade seals and gold treasures of Song and Yuan, two jade books, and one each of the ceremonial scepter, great scepter, jade belt, and jade axe.
translations.idiomatic: The new Yuan ruler fled north. Wenzhong seized his legitimate son Buyandalba along with several hundred consorts, palace women, princes, generals, ministers, and officials, fifteen jade seals and gold treasures of Song and Yuan, two jade books, and the ceremonial regalia—the scepters, jade belt, and jade axe, one of each.

sentences.zh: 出精騎窮追至北慶州而還。

translations.literal: He sent out elite cavalry in relentless pursuit as far as Northern Qingzhou and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He sent elite cavalry in pursuit all the way to Northern Qingzhou before turning back.

sentences.zh: 道興州，擒國公江文清等，降三萬七千人。

translations.literal: Passing through Xingzhou, he captured the Duke of the State Jiang Wenqing and others and accepted the surrender of thirty-seven thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Xingzhou he captured Duke of the State Jiang Wenqing and others and took the surrender of thirty-seven thousand men.

sentences.zh: 至紅羅山，又降楊思祖之眾萬六千餘人。

translations.literal: Reaching Hongluo Mountain, he again accepted the surrender of more than sixteen thousand of Yang Sizu's troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Hongluo Mountain he received the surrender of more than sixteen thousand men under Yang Sizu.

sentences.zh: 獻捷京師，帝御奉天門受朝賀。

translations.literal: He presented his victory report in the capital; the emperor took his place at the Fengtian Gate to receive the court's congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: He presented his victory in the capital, and the emperor received the court's congratulations at the Fengtian Gate.

sentences.zh: 大封功臣，文忠功最，授開國輔運推誠宣力武臣，特進榮祿大夫、右柱國、大都督府左都督，封曹國公，同知軍國事，食祿三千石，予世券。

translations.literal: The emperor enfeoffed the meritorious ministers on a great scale; Wenzhong's achievement was greatest. He was granted the title Martial Minister Who Assists the Founding, Promotes the Fortune, Extends Sincerity, and Proclaims Merit; specially promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; made Right Pillar of the State and Left Commissioner-in-Chief of the Chief Military Commission; enfeoffed as Duke of Cao; made Associate Manager of State Affairs; granted an income of three thousand piculs; and given a hereditary patent of privilege.
translations.idiomatic: In the great enfeoffment of meritorious ministers Wenzhong ranked first. He received the title Martial Minister Who Assists the Founding, Promotes the Fortune, Extends Sincerity, and Proclaims Merit; was specially promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; made Right Pillar of the State and Left Commissioner-in-Chief of the Chief Military Commission; enfeoffed as Duke of Cao with concurrent charge of state affairs; granted three thousand piculs of income; and awarded a hereditary patent of privilege.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，傅友德等平蜀，令文忠往拊循之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year, when Fu Youde and others had pacified Shu, Wenzhong was ordered to go and comfort and reassure the region.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year, after Fu Youde and others pacified Shu, Wenzhong was sent to pacify and reassure the people there.

sentences.zh: 築成都新城，發軍戍諸郡要害，乃還。

translations.literal: He built the new city of Chengdu, dispatched troops to garrison the strategic points of the various prefectures, and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He built the new walled city of Chengdu, posted troops at key points throughout the prefectures, and then returned.

sentences.zh: 明年復以左副將軍由東道北征，出居庸，趨和林，至口溫，元人遁。

translations.literal: The next year he again served as Left Vice General on a northern campaign by the eastern route, went out through Juyong, pressed toward Karakorum, reached Kökö Temür, and the Yuan men fled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he again marched north as Left Vice General by the eastern route, crossed Juyong Pass toward Karakorum, reached Kökö Temür, and the Yuan forces fled.

sentences.zh: 進至臚朐河，令部將韓政等守輜重，而自帥大軍，人齎二十日糧，疾馳至土剌河。

translations.literal: Advancing to the Luchin River, he ordered his subordinate generals Han Zheng and others to guard the baggage train, while he himself led the main army, each man carrying twenty days' rations, and galloped swiftly to the Tula River.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to the Luchin River, left Han Zheng and others to guard the baggage train, and himself led the main force—each man carrying twenty days' rations—in a forced march to the Tula River.

sentences.zh: 元太師蠻子哈剌章悉眾渡河，列騎以待。

translations.literal: The Yuan Grand Preceptor Mangqu Harachin brought his entire force across the river and drew up his cavalry in line to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan Grand Preceptor Mangqu Harachin brought his whole army across the river and drew up his cavalry to meet them.

sentences.zh: 文忠引軍薄之，敵稍卻。

translations.literal: Wenzhong led his army close against them, and the enemy drew back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong pressed his army forward; the enemy gave ground.

sentences.zh: 至阿魯渾河，敵來益眾。

translations.literal: Reaching the Aruhun River, the enemy came in ever greater numbers.
translations.idiomatic: At the Aruhun River the enemy forces grew ever thicker.

sentences.zh: 文忠馬中流矢，下馬持短兵鬥。

translations.literal: Wenzhong's horse was struck by a flying arrow; he dismounted and fought with short weapons.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow struck his mount. He dismounted and fought on foot with a short weapon.

sentences.zh: 指揮李榮以所乘馬授文忠，而自奪敵馬乘之。

translations.literal: The commander Li Rong gave Wenzhong the horse he himself rode, while seizing an enemy horse for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Li Rong gave Wenzhong his own horse and wrested a mount from the enemy for himself.

sentences.zh: 文忠得馬，益殊死戰，遂破敵，虜獲萬計。

translations.literal: Wenzhong, having obtained a horse, fought all the more desperately to the death and thus broke the enemy, capturing and taking booty by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Mounted again, Wenzhong fought with redoubled fury and routed the enemy, taking captives and booty by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 追奔至稱海，敵兵復大集。

translations.literal: Pursuing the fleeing enemy to Chenghai, the enemy troops again gathered in great force.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit carried to Chenghai, where the enemy massed again in strength.

sentences.zh: 文忠乃斂兵據險，椎牛饗士，縱所獲馬畜於野。

translations.literal: Wenzhong then drew in his troops and held a defensible position, slaughtered oxen to feast his men, and turned loose the captured horses and livestock on the plain.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his men into strong ground, feasted them on slaughtered oxen, and turned the captured herds loose on the plain.

sentences.zh: 敵疑有伏，稍稍引去。

translations.literal: The enemy suspected an ambush and gradually withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy suspected an ambush and slowly drew off.

sentences.zh: 文忠亦引還，失故道。

translations.literal: Wenzhong also led his force back, but lost the former road.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong withdrew as well, but lost his way.

sentences.zh: 至桑哥兒麻，乏水，渴甚，禱於天。

translations.literal: Reaching Sanggermah, they lacked water and were extremely thirsty; he prayed to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At Sanggermah they ran out of water and were parched with thirst; he prayed to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 所乘馬跑地，泉湧出，三軍皆給，乃刑牲以祭。

translations.literal: The horse he rode pawed the ground and a spring gushed forth; the whole army was supplied, and he then slaughtered animals to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: His horse pawed the earth and a spring burst forth. The whole army was saved. He sacrificed animals in thanks.

sentences.zh: 遂還。

translations.literal: He then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Then he marched home.

sentences.zh: 是役也，兩軍勝負相當，而宣甯侯曹良臣，指揮使周顯、常榮、張耀俱戰死，以故賞不行。

translations.literal: In this campaign the two sides' victory and defeat were roughly equal, but Marquis of Xuanning Cao Liangchen and the commanders Zhou Xian, Chang Rong, and Zhang Yao all died in battle; for this reason rewards were not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In that campaign both sides could claim something like a draw, yet Marquis of Xuanning Cao Liangchen and the commanders Zhou Xian, Chang Rong, and Zhang Yao all fell in battle, so no rewards were issued.

sentences.zh: 六年行北平、山西邊，敗敵於三角村。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he conducted operations along the Beiping and Shanxi frontier and defeated the enemy at Sanjiao Village.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he patrolled the Beiping and Shanxi frontier and defeated the enemy at Sanjiao Village.

sentences.zh: 七年遣部將分道出塞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he sent subordinate generals on separate routes beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he sent subordinate generals on separate sorties beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 至三不剌川，俘平章陳安禮。

translations.literal: Reaching the Sanbula River, he captured the Pacification Commissioner Chen Anli.
translations.idiomatic: At the Sanbula River he captured Pacification Commissioner Chen Anli.

sentences.zh: 至順甯、楊門，斬真珠驢。

translations.literal: Reaching Shunning and Yangmen, he beheaded Zhenzhulu.
translations.idiomatic: At Shunning and Yangmen he slew Zhenzhulu.

sentences.zh: 至白登，擒太尉不花。

translations.literal: Reaching Baideng, he captured the Grand Marshal Buhua.
translations.idiomatic: At Baideng he took Grand Marshal Buhua prisoner.

sentences.zh: 其秋帥師攻大寧、高州，克之，斬宗王朵朵失裏，擒承旨百家奴。

translations.literal: That autumn he led his army to attack Daning and Gaozhou, took them, beheaded the prince Duoduoshili, and captured the Grand Secretary Baijianu.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he attacked Daning and Gaozhou, captured both, slew Prince Duoduoshili, and took Grand Secretary Baijianu prisoner.

sentences.zh: 追奔至氈帽山，擊斬魯王，獲其妃及司徒答海等。

translations.literal: Pursuing the fleeing enemy to Zhanmao Mountain, he struck and slew the Prince of Lu and captured his consort and the Minister of Works Dahai and others.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit reached Zhanmao Mountain, where he killed the Prince of Lu and seized his consort, Minister of Works Dahai, and others.

sentences.zh: 進師豐州，擒元故官十二人，馬駝牛羊甚眾，窮追至百幹兒乃還。

translations.literal: Advancing to Fengzhou, he captured twelve former Yuan officials, and horses, camels, cattle, and sheep in great numbers; he pursued to the limit at Baiganer and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Fengzhou, took twelve former Yuan officials, and vast herds of horses, camels, cattle, and sheep, pursuing as far as Baiganer before turning back.

sentences.zh: 是後屢出備邊。

translations.literal: After this he went out repeatedly to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: After that he campaigned repeatedly on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 十年命與韓國公李善長議軍國重事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered to deliberate on weighty military and state affairs together with the Duke of Han Li Shanchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was ordered to join the Duke of Han, Li Shanchang, in deliberating on major affairs of state and war.

sentences.zh: 十二年，洮州十八番族叛，與西平侯沐英合兵討平之，築城東籠山南川，置洮州衛。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the eighteen Fan tribes of Taozhou rebelled; together with the Marquis of Xiping Mu Ying he combined forces to suppress and pacify them, built a city south of the eastern ridge of Donglong Mountain in the southern pass, and established Taozhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the eighteen Fan tribes of Taozhou rebelled. With Marquis of Xiping Mu Ying he suppressed them, built a city south of Donglong Mountain's eastern ridge, and established Taozhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 還言西安城中水鹼鹵不可飲，請鑿地引龍首渠入城以便汲，從之。

translations.literal: On his return he reported that the water in the city of Xi'an was brackish and undrinkable and asked to dig and draw in the Longshou Canal to make drawing water convenient; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported that Xi'an's water was brackish and undrinkable and asked to tap the Longshou Canal into the city; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 還掌大都督府兼領國子監事。

translations.literal: On his return he again took charge of the Chief Military Commission and concurrently headed the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He resumed charge of the Chief Military Commission and concurrently directed the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 文忠器量沉宏，人莫測其際。

translations.literal: Wenzhong's capacity was deep and vast; no one could fathom his inner reaches.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong's bearing was deep and immeasurable; no one could plumb his inner mind.

sentences.zh: 臨陣踔厲曆風發，遇大敵益壯。

translations.literal: In battle he was impetuous and swift as a rising wind; when he met a great enemy he grew all the sterner.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he surged forward like a rising gale, and the greater the foe the fiercer he became.

sentences.zh: 頗好學問，常師事金華范祖幹、胡翰，通曉經義，為詩歌雄駿可觀。

translations.literal: He was quite fond of learning; he regularly took as teachers Fan Zugan and Hu Han of Jinhua, mastered the classics, and his poetry was bold and imposing, worthy of admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, studied under Fan Zugan and Hu Han of Jinhua, mastered the classics, and wrote poetry of bold, striking force.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖定應天，以軍興不給，增民田租，文忠請之，得減額。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Founder secured Yingtian, because military campaigns could not be supplied he increased the land tax on the people; Wenzhong petitioned on their behalf and the levy was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took Yingtian, war costs drove him to raise the land tax. Wenzhong petitioned for relief and the levy was cut.

sentences.zh: 其釋兵家居，恂恂若儒者，帝雅愛重之。

translations.literal: When he laid aside his arms and lived at home he was respectful and mild like a scholar; the emperor cherished and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: At home in retirement he was courteous and mild as a scholar, and the emperor held him in special regard.

sentences.zh: 家故多客，嘗以客言，勸帝少誅戮，又諫帝征日本，及言宦者過盛，非天子不近刑人之義。

translations.literal: His household had long kept many guests; he once used a guest's words to urge the emperor to execute fewer people, again remonstrated against the campaign against Japan, and spoke of the excessive number of eunuchs, contrary to the principle that the Son of Heaven should not keep men subject to corporal punishment close at hand.
translations.idiomatic: His house had long entertained many guests. Through them he urged the emperor to kill less, opposed the Japanese campaign, and warned that too many eunuchs violated the principle that the Son of Heaven should not keep men subject to mutilation close at hand.

sentences.zh: 以是積忤旨，不免譴責。

translations.literal: For these reasons he repeatedly offended the imperial will and could not escape reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: Such counsel repeatedly offended the throne and brought him reprimand.

sentences.zh: 十六年冬遂得疾。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixteenth year he finally fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixteenth year he fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 帝親臨視，使淮安侯華中護醫藥。

translations.literal: The emperor came in person to visit him and sent the Marquis of Huai'an Hua Zhong to oversee his medical care.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited him in person and sent Marquis of Huai'an Hua Zhong to supervise his treatment.

sentences.zh: 明年三月卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year he died, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following third month, aged forty-six.

sentences.zh: 帝疑中毒之，貶中爵，放其家屬于建昌衛，諸醫並妻子皆斬。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected poisoning; he degraded Zhong's title, exiled his household to Jianchang Guard, and executed all the physicians together with their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected poison. He degraded Hua Zhong, exiled the household to Jianchang Guard, and executed the physicians and their families.

sentences.zh: 親為文致祭，追封岐陽王，諡武靖。

translations.literal: He personally composed a text to offer sacrifice, posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Qiyang, and gave the posthumous title Wujing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote the sacrificial text himself, posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Qiyang, and gave him the posthumous name Wujing.

sentences.zh: 配享太廟，肖像功臣廟，位皆第三。

translations.literal: He was granted a place in the Imperial Ancestral Temple sacrifices and a portrait in the Hall of Meritorious Ministers, in both cases in the third position.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a place in the Imperial Ancestral Temple sacrifices and a portrait in the Hall of Meritorious Ministers, each in the third rank.

sentences.zh: 父貞前卒，贈隴西王，諡恭獻。

translations.literal: His father Zhen had died earlier and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Longxi with the posthumous title Gongxian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen had died earlier and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Longxi with the posthumous name Gongxian.

sentences.zh: 文忠三子，長景隆，次增枝、芳英，皆帝賜名。

translations.literal: Wenzhong had three sons: the eldest Jinglong, the second Zengzhi, and Fangying; all received names bestowed by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong had three sons: Jinglong the eldest, then Zengzhi and Fangying, all given their names by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 增枝初授勳衛，擢前軍左都督。

translations.literal: Zengzhi was first appointed to the Guard of Meritorious Service and was promoted to Left Commissioner-in-Chief of the Vanguard Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zengzhi first served in the Guard of Meritorious Service and rose to Left Commissioner-in-Chief of the Vanguard Army.

sentences.zh: 芳英官至中都正留守。

translations.literal: Fangying rose to the post of Chief Defender of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fangying became Chief Defender of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 景隆，小字九江。

translations.literal: Jinglong, childhood name Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglong, whose childhood name was Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 讀書通典故。

translations.literal: In reading he was versed in precedent and ancient matters.
translations.idiomatic: In his studies he mastered precedent and classical allusion.

sentences.zh: 長身，眉目疏秀，顧盼偉然。

translations.literal: Tall in stature, with sparse, refined brows and eyes, his glances were imposing.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall, with refined brows and eyes, and carried himself with imposing presence.

sentences.zh: 每朝會，進止雍容甚都，太祖數目屬之。

translations.literal: At each court assembly his advance and withdrawal were dignified and elegant; the Founder often fixed his gaze on him.
translations.idiomatic: At court his bearing was dignified and graceful, and the Founder often fixed his gaze on him.

sentences.zh: 十九年襲爵，屢出練軍湖廣、陝西、河南，市馬西番。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he inherited the title and went out repeatedly to drill troops in Huguang, Shaanxi, and Henan and to purchase horses in the Western Territories.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he inherited the title, repeatedly drilled troops in Huguang, Shaanxi, and Henan, and bought horses in the Western Territories.

sentences.zh: 進掌左軍都督府事，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: He was advanced to take charge of the Left Military Commission and was additionally made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in charge of the Left Military Commission and made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 建文帝即位，景隆以肺腑見親任，嘗被命執周王橚。

translations.literal: When the Jianwen Emperor ascended the throne, Jinglong was treated with intimate trust as a close kinsman and was once ordered to arrest Prince Zhou Zhu Su.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jianwen Emperor came to the throne, Jinglong was trusted as close kin and once ordered to arrest Prince of Zhou Zhu Su.

sentences.zh: 及燕兵起，長興侯耿炳文討燕失利，齊泰、黃子澄等共薦景隆。

translations.literal: When the Yan armies rose, the Marquis of Changxing Geng Bingwen campaigned against Yan and met defeat; Qi Tai, Huang Zicheng, and others together recommended Jinglong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan rebelled, Marquis of Changxing Geng Bingwen was defeated in the northern campaign; Qi Tai, Huang Zicheng, and others recommended Jinglong in his place.

sentences.zh: 乃以景隆代炳文為大將軍，將兵五十萬北伐。

translations.literal: Jinglong was then made Great General in Bingwen's stead and led five hundred thousand troops on a northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglong replaced Bingwen as Great General and marched north with five hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 賜通天犀帶，帝親為推輪，餞之江滸，令一切便宜行事。

translations.literal: He was granted a belt of penetrating-heaven rhinoceros horn; the emperor personally pushed the wheel of his chariot, feasted him on the riverbank, and ordered him to act at his own discretion in all matters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him a belt of penetrating-heaven rhinoceros horn, pushed his chariot wheel in farewell at the riverbank, and authorized him to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 景隆貴公子，不知兵，惟自尊大，諸宿將多怏怏不為用。

translations.literal: Jinglong was a nobleman's son who knew nothing of warfare and was arrogant alone; the veteran generals were mostly resentful and unwilling to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglong was a pampered noble who knew nothing of war and lorded it over his betters; the veteran generals resented him and would not follow willingly.

sentences.zh: 景隆馳至德州，會兵進營河間。

translations.literal: Jinglong galloped to Dezhou, joined forces, and advanced to encamp at Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped to Dezhou, gathered his forces, and advanced to camp at Hejian.

sentences.zh: 燕王聞之喜，語諸將曰：「李九江，紈綺少年耳，易與也。」

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan heard this he was pleased and said to his generals: "Li Jiujiang is but a silken-clad youth, easy to deal with."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan was delighted and told his generals, "Li Jiujiang is only a silken youth—easy prey."

sentences.zh: 遂命世子居守，戒勿出戰，而自引兵援永平，直趨大寧。

translations.literal: He then ordered the heir to remain on guard, admonished him not to go out to battle, and himself led troops to relieve Yongping and pressed straight toward Daning.
translations.idiomatic: He left the heir to hold the city, forbade him to give battle, and marched himself to relieve Yongping and seize Daning.

sentences.zh: 景隆聞之，進圍北平。

translations.literal: When Jinglong heard this he advanced to besiege Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglong heard and advanced to besiege Beiping.

sentences.zh: 都督瞿能攻張掖門，垂破。

translations.literal: The Commissioner-in-Chief Qu Neng attacked the Zhangye Gate and was on the verge of breaking through.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner-in-Chief Qu Neng attacked the Zhangye Gate and nearly broke through.

sentences.zh: 景隆忌能功，止之。

translations.literal: Jinglong, jealous of Neng's achievement, stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglong, jealous of his success, ordered him to halt.

sentences.zh: 及燕師破大寧，還軍擊景隆。

translations.literal: When the Yan army took Daning and returned to strike Jinglong,
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan forces took Daning and turned back against Jinglong,

sentences.zh: 景隆屢大敗，奔德州，諸軍皆潰。

translations.literal: Jinglong was repeatedly defeated and fled to Dezhou; all the armies dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglong suffered repeated defeats and fled to Dezhou while his armies collapsed.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，燕王攻大同，景隆引軍出紫荊關往救，無功而還。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year the Prince of Yan attacked Datong; Jinglong led his army out through Zijing Pass to relieve it but achieved nothing and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next first month the Prince of Yan struck Datong. Jinglong marched through Zijing Pass to relieve it, accomplished nothing, and returned.

sentences.zh: 帝慮景隆權尚輕，遣中官齎璽書賜黃鉞弓矢，專征伐。

translations.literal: The emperor feared Jinglong's authority was still too light and sent a palace eunuch bearing an imperial seal and edict to bestow the yellow battle-axe and bow and arrows, with sole authority over campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Jinglong still lacked authority, the emperor sent a eunuch with an imperial seal, the yellow battle-axe, and bow and arrows, granting him sole command.

sentences.zh: 方渡江，風雨舟壞，賜物盡失，乃更制以賜。

translations.literal: Just as he was crossing the river, wind and rain wrecked the boats and the gifts were all lost; new ones were then made and bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the river, a storm wrecked his boats and the gifts were lost; replacements were made and sent.

sentences.zh: 四月，景隆大誓師於德州，會武定侯郭英、安陸侯吳傑等於真定，合軍六十萬，進營白溝河。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Jinglong held a great oath-taking at Dezhou, joined the Marquis of Wuding Guo Ying, the Marquis of Anlu Wu Jie, and others at Zhending, combined six hundred thousand troops, and advanced to encamp at the Baigou River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he swore a great oath at Dezhou, joined Marquis of Wuding Guo Ying, Marquis of Anlu Wu Jie, and others at Zhending with six hundred thousand men, and camped on the Baigou River.

sentences.zh: 與燕軍連戰，復大敗，璽書斧鉞皆委棄，走德州，復走濟南。

translations.literal: In continuous battles with the Yan army he was again greatly defeated; the imperial seal, edict, axe, and battle-axe were all abandoned; he fled to Dezhou and again to Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Battle after battle ended in rout. He abandoned the imperial seal, edict, axe, and regalia, fled to Dezhou, then to Jinan.

sentences.zh: 斯役也，王師死者數十萬人，南軍遂不支，帝始詔景隆還。

translations.literal: In this campaign several hundred thousand imperial troops died; the southern armies could no longer hold, and the emperor at last ordered Jinglong to return.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of thousands of imperial troops died in that campaign. The southern armies could no longer hold, and the emperor recalled Jinglong.

sentences.zh: 黃子澄慚憤，執景隆于朝班，請誅之以謝天下。

translations.literal: Huang Zicheng, ashamed and enraged, seized Jinglong in the court ranks and asked that he be executed to appease the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zicheng, shamed and furious, seized Jinglong in court and demanded his execution to appease the realm.

sentences.zh: 燕師渡江，帝旁皇甚，方孝孺復請誅景隆。

translations.literal: When the Yan army crossed the Yangzi the emperor was in great distress; Fang Xiaoru again asked that Jinglong be executed.
translations.idiomatic: As the Yan army crossed the Yangzi the emperor was desperate; Fang Xiaoru again demanded Jinglong's death.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不問。

translations.literal: The emperor in both cases did not inquire further.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused both times.

sentences.zh: 使景隆及尚書茹瑺、都督王佐如燕軍，割地請和。

translations.literal: He sent Jinglong together with the Minister of Revenue Ru Yao and Commissioner-in-Chief Wang Zuo to the Yan army to cede territory and sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Jinglong with Minister of Revenue Ru Yao and Commissioner-in-Chief Wang Zuo to the Yan camp to offer territory and sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 燕兵屯金川門，景隆與谷王橞開門迎降。

translations.literal: When the Yan army encamped at the Jinchuan Gate, Jinglong and Prince Gu Zhu Hui opened the gate to welcome their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army reached the Jinchuan Gate, Jinglong and Prince Gu Zhu Hui opened the gates in surrender.

sentences.zh: 燕王即帝位，授景隆奉天輔運推誠宣力武臣、特進光祿大夫、左柱國，增歲祿千石。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan took the throne he appointed Jinglong Martial Minister Who Assists Heaven, Promotes the Fortune, Extends Sincerity, and Proclaims Merit; specially promoted to Grand Master of Glorious Blessings; made Left Pillar of the State; and increased his annual stipend by a thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan became emperor he confirmed Jinglong as Martial Minister Who Assists Heaven, Promotes the Fortune, Extends Sincerity, and Proclaims Merit, made him Grand Master of Glorious Blessings and Left Pillar of the State, and added a thousand piculs to his income.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有大事，景隆猶以班首主議，諸功臣咸不平。

translations.literal: When the court had great affairs Jinglong still took the lead in deliberation as foremost in rank; the meritorious ministers were all discontented.
translations.idiomatic: On great state occasions Jinglong still spoke first among the ministers, to the resentment of the founding generals.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年，周王發其建文時至邸受賂事，刑部尚書鄭賜等亦劾景隆包藏禍心，蓄養亡命，謀為不軌。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle the Prince of Zhou exposed his acceptance of bribes at his residence during the Jianwen reign; the Minister of Justice Zheng Ci and others also impeached Jinglong for harboring a treacherous heart, keeping fugitives, and plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 2 the Prince of Zhou exposed bribes Jinglong had taken during the Jianwen years; Minister of Justice Zheng Ci and others impeached him for treason, sheltering fugitives, and plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 詔勿問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that the matter not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the charges dropped.

sentences.zh: 已，成國公硃能、吏部尚書蹇義與文武群臣，廷劾景隆及弟增枝逆謀有狀，六科給事中張信等復劾之。

translations.literal: Afterward the Duke of Cheng Zhu Neng, the Minister of Personnel Jian Yi, and the civil and military officials impeached Jinglong and his younger brother Zengzhi together in court for manifest treason; the supervising secretaries of the Six Offices headed by Zhang Xin impeached them again.
translations.idiomatic: Later Duke of Cheng Zhu Neng, Minister of Personnel Jian Yi, and the civil and military officials jointly impeached Jinglong and Zengzhi in open court; supervising secretaries led by Zhang Xin impeached them again.

sentences.zh: 詔削勳號，絕朝請，以公歸第，奉長公主祀。

translations.literal: An edict stripped his title of merit, cut off his attendance at court, and sent him home as a duke to perform sacrifices for the Senior Princess.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of his merit title, barred from court, and sent home as a duke to tend the Senior Princess's rites.

sentences.zh: 亡何，禮部尚書李至剛等復言：「景隆在家，坐受閽人伏謁如君臣禮，大不道；

translations.literal: Before long the Minister of Rites Li Zhigang and others again reported: "Jinglong at home sits receiving obeisance from gatekeepers as though they were subject and ruler, a grave offense;
translations.idiomatic: Soon Minister of Rites Li Zhigang reported that Jinglong at home received obeisance from his gatekeepers as from subjects to a ruler,

sentences.zh: 增枝多立莊田，蓄僮僕無慮千百，意叵測。」

translations.literal: Zengzhi has established many estate fields and keeps bond servants numbering no less than a thousand or several thousand; his intentions cannot be fathomed."
translations.idiomatic: while Zengzhi amassed estates and kept bond servants by the thousands, their intentions beyond reckoning."

sentences.zh: 於是奪景隆爵，並增枝及妻子數十人錮私第，沒其財產。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jinglong's title was taken away, and Zengzhi together with his wife and children, several tens of persons, were imprisoned in a private residence while their property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglong was stripped of his rank; Zengzhi, his wife, children, and dozens of kin were imprisoned at home and their property seized.

sentences.zh: 景隆嘗絕食旬日不死，至永樂末乃卒。

translations.literal: Jinglong once fasted for ten days yet did not die; only at the end of Yongle did he finally perish.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglong once fasted ten days without dying; he finally expired only at the end of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年始下詔令增枝等啟門第，得自便。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong an edict at last ordered Zengzhi and the others to open their gates and go where they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 13 an edict finally let Zengzhi and the others leave their confinement freely.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，錄文忠後，以景隆曾孫璿為南京錦衣衛世指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi the descendants of Wenzhong were recorded; Jinglong's great-grandson Xuan was made hereditary Commander of the Nanjing Brocade Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi Wenzhong's line was restored; Jinglong's great-grandson Xuan became hereditary Commander of the Nanjing Brocade Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，子濂嗣。

translations.literal: When he died his son Lian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died and his son Lian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 卒，子性嗣。

translations.literal: When he died his son Xing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died and his son Xing succeeded.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年詔封性為臨淮侯，祿千石。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiajing an edict enfeoffed Xing as Marquis of Linhuai with an income of a thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 11 an edict enfeoffed Xing as Marquis of Linhuai with a thousand piculs of income.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒，無子，復以濂弟沂紹封。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died without a son, and Lian's younger brother Yi was again enfeoffed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He died within a year without an heir, and Lian's younger brother Yi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 卒，子庭竹嗣。

translations.literal: When he died his son Tingshu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died and his son Tingshu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 屢典軍府，提督操江，佩平蠻將軍印，鎮湖廣。

translations.literal: He repeatedly directed military offices, supervised training on the Yangzi, bore the seal of the Pacification General, and garrisoned Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly directed military offices, supervised Yangzi training, bore the Pacification General's seal, and garrisoned Huguang.

sentences.zh: 卒，子言恭嗣。

translations.literal: When he died his son Yangong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died and his son Yangong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 守備南京，入督京營，累加少保。

translations.literal: He defended Nanjing, entered to supervise the capital garrison, and was repeatedly promoted to Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He defended Nanjing, supervised the capital garrison, and rose to Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 言恭，字惟寅，好學能詩，折節寒素。

translations.literal: Yangong, courtesy name Weiyin, loved learning and could write poetry; he lowered himself to treat the poor with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Yangong, courtesy name Weiyin, loved learning and poetry and treated the poor with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 子宗城，少以文學知名。

translations.literal: His son Zongcheng was known from youth for literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongcheng was known early for literary talent.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，倭犯朝鮮，兵部尚書石星主封貢，薦宗城才，授都督僉事，充正使，持節往，指揮楊方亨副之。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign, when the Japanese invaded Korea, the Minister of War Shi Xing favored investiture and tribute; he recommended Zongcheng's talent, appointed him Vice Commissioner-in-Chief, made him chief envoy bearing credentials, and sent him forth; the commander Yang Fangheng served as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign, when Japan invaded Korea, Minister of War Shi Xing favored tribute and investiture, recommended Zongcheng, appointed him Vice Commissioner-in-Chief and chief envoy with credentials, and sent Commander Yang Fangheng as deputy.

sentences.zh: 宗城至朝鮮釜山，倭來益眾，道路籍籍，言且劫二使。

translations.literal: Zongcheng reached Pusan in Korea; the Japanese came in ever greater numbers, and along the roads there was widespread talk that the two envoys would soon be seized.
translations.idiomatic: Zongcheng reached Pusan in Korea as Japanese forces grew; rumor spread that the envoys would be seized.

sentences.zh: 宗城恐，變服逃歸。

translations.literal: Zongcheng was afraid, changed his clothes, and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zongcheng disguised himself and fled home.

sentences.zh: 而方亨渡海，為倭所辱。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Fangheng crossed the sea and was humiliated by the Japanese.
translations.idiomatic: Fangheng crossed the sea and was shamed by the Japanese.

sentences.zh: 宗城下獄論戍，以其子邦鎮嗣侯。

translations.literal: Zongcheng was imprisoned, sentenced to penal service, and his son Bangzhen inherited the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Zongcheng was imprisoned and sentenced to exile; his son Bangzhen inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 明亡，爵絕。

translations.literal: When the Ming perished the enfeoffment came to an end.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming fell, the line ended.

sentences.zh: 鄧愈，虹人。

translations.literal: Deng Yu was a native of Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yu came from Hong County.

sentences.zh: 初名友德，太祖為賜名。

translations.literal: His original name was Youde; the Founder bestowed upon him the name [Yu].
translations.idiomatic: He was originally named Youde; the Founder gave him the name Yu.

sentences.zh: 父順興，據臨濠，與元兵戰死，兄友隆代之，復病死，眾推愈領軍事。

translations.literal: His father Shunxing held Linhao, died fighting the Yuan troops, and his elder brother Youlong replaced him but again died of illness; the multitude pushed Yu to take command of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shunxing had held Linhao and was killed fighting Yuan forces. His elder brother Youlong took over but soon died of illness, and the troops pressed Yu to assume command.

sentences.zh: 愈年甫十六，每戰必先登陷陣，軍中鹹服其勇。

translations.literal: Yu was only sixteen; in every battle he was always first to ascend and break into the enemy ranks, and throughout the army all submitted to his courage.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was only sixteen, yet in every battle he was the first to charge the enemy lines, and the whole army came to respect his valor.

sentences.zh: 太祖起滁陽，愈自盱眙來歸，授管軍總管。

translations.literal: When the Founder rose at Chuyang, Yu came from Xuyi to join him and was appointed Military Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder raised his banner at Chuyang, Yu came from Xuyi to join him and was made Military Commandant.

sentences.zh: 從渡江。

translations.literal: He followed in crossing the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi with the army.

sentences.zh: 克太平，破擒陳野先，略定溧陽、溧水，下集慶，取鎮江，皆有功。

translations.literal: He captured Taiping, routed and seized Chen Yexian, pacified Liyang and Lishui, took Jiqing, and seized Zhenjiang—at all of these he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He helped capture Taiping, defeat and seize Chen Yexian, pacify Liyang and Lishui, take Jiqing, and seize Zhenjiang, distinguishing himself in each campaign.

sentences.zh: 進廣興翼元帥，出守廣德州，破長槍帥謝國璽於城下，俘其總管武世榮，獲甲士千人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Marshal of the Broad Expansion Wing, went out to garrison Guangde Prefecture, defeated the Long Spear chieftain Xie Guoxi beneath the walls, captured his commandant Wu Shirong, and obtained a thousand armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Marshal of the Broad Expansion Wing, he garrisoned Guangde Prefecture, routed the Long Spear chieftain Xie Guoxi beneath the walls, captured his commandant Wu Shirong, and took a thousand armored troops.

sentences.zh: 移鎮宣州，以其兵取績溪，與胡大海克徽州，遷行樞密院判官守之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison Xuanzhou, took Jixi with his troops, together with Hu Dahai captured Huizhou, and was promoted to Acting Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to garrison Xuanzhou, he seized Jixi with his own forces, joined Hu Dahai in capturing Huizhou, and was promoted to Acting Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 苗帥楊完者以十萬眾來攻，守禦單弱，愈激勵將士，與大海合擊，破走之。

translations.literal: The Miao chieftain Yang Wanzhe came to attack with a hundred thousand men; the defense was thin and weak, but Yu roused the officers and soldiers, joined with Dahai in a combined strike, and routed and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao chieftain Yang Wanzhe attacked with a hundred thousand men, the garrison was badly outnumbered; Yu rallied his troops, joined Hu Dahai in a combined assault, and drove the enemy off.

sentences.zh: 進拔休寧、婺源，獲卒三千，徇下高河壘。

translations.literal: Advancing, he captured Xiuning and Wuyuan, obtained three thousand soldiers, and marched to reduce the fort at Gaohe.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to take Xiuning and Wuyuan, captured three thousand troops, and subdued the fort at Gaohe.

sentences.zh: 與李文忠、胡大海攻建德，道遂安，破長槍帥餘子貞，逐北至淳安，又破其援兵，遂克建德。

translations.literal: Together with Li Wenzhong and Hu Dahai he attacked Jiande, passed through Suian, defeated the Long Spear chieftain Yu Zizhen, pursued north to Chun'an, again defeated his relief force, and thereby captured Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Wenzhong and Hu Dahai he attacked Jiande, routed the Long Spear chieftain Yu Zizhen at Suian, pursued him north to Chun'an, smashed his reinforcements, and finally took Jiande.

sentences.zh: 楊完者來攻，破擒其將李副樞，降溪洞兵三萬。

translations.literal: Yang Wanzhe came to attack; he routed and captured his general Vice Censor-in-Chief Li and accepted the surrender of thirty thousand stream-cave troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Wanzhe attacked again, he routed and captured his general Vice Censor-in-Chief Li and received the surrender of thirty thousand indigenous troops.

sentences.zh: 逾月，復破完者于烏龍嶺。

translations.literal: After more than a month he again defeated Wanzhe at Wulong Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he defeated Wanzhe again at Wulong Ridge.

sentences.zh: 再遷僉行樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was again transferred and made Associate Commissioner of the Acting Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He received a further promotion to Associate Commissioner of the Acting Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 略臨安，李伯升來援，敗之閑林寨。

translations.literal: He reduced Lin'an; Li Bosheng came to relieve it, and he defeated him at Xianlin Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He subdued Lin'an; when Li Bosheng marched to its relief, he routed him at Xianlin Stockade.

sentences.zh: 遣使說降饒州守將於光，遂移守饒。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to persuade Yu Guang, the defending general of Raozhou, to surrender, and then transferred to garrison Rao.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to persuade Raozhou's defender Yu Guang to surrender, then moved to garrison the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 饒濱彭蠡湖，與友諒接境，數來侵，輒擊卻之。

translations.literal: Rao bordered Poyang Lake and adjoined Youliang's territory; the enemy came repeatedly to raid, and each time he struck and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Raozhou lay on Poyang Lake and bordered Chen Youliang's domain; whenever the enemy raided, he beat them back.

sentences.zh: 進江南行省參政，總制各翼軍馬。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Administrative Vice Commissioner of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat and given overall command of the armies of the various wings.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Administrative Vice Commissioner of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat, he took overall command of the wing armies.

sentences.zh: 取浮梁，徇樂平，餘幹、建昌皆下。

translations.literal: He took Fuliang, marched on Leping, and Yuyu and Jianchang all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Fuliang, subdued Leping, and brought Yuyu and Jianchang under control.

sentences.zh: 友諒撫州守將鄧克明為吳宏所攻，遣使偽降以緩師。

translations.literal: Youliang's defending general of Fuzhou, Deng Keming, was being attacked by Wu Hong and sent envoys in a feigned surrender to delay the army.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youliang's Fuzhou defender Deng Keming, besieged by Wu Hong, sent envoys feigning surrender to stall the attack.

sentences.zh: 愈知其情，卷甲夜馳二百里，比明入其城。

translations.literal: Yu knew his intent, wrapped his armor and galloped two hundred li by night, and by dawn entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yu saw through the ruse, wrapped his armor and rode two hundred li through the night, entering the city at dawn.

sentences.zh: 克明出不意，單騎走。

translations.literal: Keming, caught unawares, fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Taken completely by surprise, Keming fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 愈號令嚴肅，秋毫不犯，遂定撫州。

translations.literal: Yu kept his orders strict and disciplined, not violating so much as an autumn hair, and thereby settled Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu enforced strict discipline and forbade the slightest looting, and so secured Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 克明不得已降。

translations.literal: Keming, having no alternative, surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Keming had no choice but to surrender.

sentences.zh: 會友諒丞相胡廷瑞獻龍興路，改洪都府，以愈為江西行省參政守之，而命降將祝宗、康泰以所部從。

translations.literal: It happened that Youliang's chancellor Hu Tingrui presented Longxing Circuit, which was changed to Hongdu Prefecture; Yu was made Administrative Vice Commissioner of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat to defend it, and the surrendered generals Zhu Zong and Kang Tai were ordered to follow with their troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youliang's chancellor Hu Tingrui surrendered Longxing Circuit, renamed Hongdu Prefecture, Yu was made Administrative Vice Commissioner of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat to hold it, with the surrendered generals Zhu Zong and Kang Tai ordered to follow with their troops.

sentences.zh: 二人初不欲降，及奉命從徐達攻武昌，遂反。

translations.literal: The two at first had not wished to surrender; when ordered to follow Xu Da in attacking Wuchang, they thereupon rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The two had never truly wished to submit; ordered to join Xu Da's assault on Wuchang, they rebelled.

sentences.zh: 舟次女兒港，趨還，乘夜破新城門而入。

translations.literal: When their boats reached Daughters' Harbor they hurried back, broke through the New City Gate by night, and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Their fleet had reached Daughters' Harbor when they turned back, broke through the New City Gate under cover of night, and seized the city.

sentences.zh: 愈倉卒聞變，以數十騎走，數與賊遇。

translations.literal: Yu, hearing of the upheaval in haste, fled with several dozen horsemen and several times encountered the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yu learned of the revolt in sudden alarm and fled with a few dozen horsemen, clashing repeatedly with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 從騎死且盡，窘甚。

translations.literal: His accompanying riders were nearly all dead, and he was in extreme straits.
translations.idiomatic: His escort was nearly wiped out, and he was in desperate peril.

sentences.zh: 連易三馬，馬輒踣。

translations.literal: He changed horses three times in succession, and each horse immediately fell.
translations.idiomatic: He changed mounts three times in a row, and each horse collapsed beneath him.

sentences.zh: 最後得養子馬乘之，始得奪撫州門以出，奔還應天。

translations.literal: At last he obtained his adopted son's horse and rode it; only then was he able to seize the Fuzhou Gate and get out, fleeing back to Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: At last he mounted his adopted son's horse, broke through the Fuzhou Gate, and escaped back to Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 太祖弗之罪也。

translations.literal: The Founder did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder did not hold it against him.

sentences.zh: 既而徐達還師復洪都，復命愈佐大都督硃文正鎮之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Xu Da returned his army and recovered Hongdu; Yu was again ordered to assist the Grand Commander Zhu Wenzhong in garrisoning it.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Da marched back and retook Hongdu, Yu was again ordered to assist Grand Commander Zhu Wenzhong in its defense.

sentences.zh: 其明年，友諒眾六十萬入寇，樓船高與城等，乘漲直抵城下，圍數百重。

translations.literal: The next year Youliang's force of six hundred thousand invaded; his tower ships were as tall as the walls, and riding the flood they came straight to the foot of the city, encircling it in hundreds of rings.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Chen Youliang invaded with six hundred thousand men; his tower ships stood as high as the walls, and riding the flood they swept straight to the city, wrapping it in layer upon layer of siege.

sentences.zh: 愈分守撫州門，當要衝。

translations.literal: Yu was assigned to defend the Fuzhou Gate, standing at the vital crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was posted at the Fuzhou Gate, the city's most critical point.

sentences.zh: 友諒親督眾來攻，城壞且三十餘丈，愈且築且戰。

translations.literal: Youliang personally directed his multitude in the attack; the wall was breached to nearly thirty-plus zhang, and Yu both repaired and fought.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youliang personally led the assault; the wall was breached for more than thirty zhang, yet Yu fought on even as he rebuilt it.

sentences.zh: 敵攻益急，晝夜不解甲者三月。

translations.literal: The enemy's assault grew ever fiercer; for three months day and night they did not remove their armor.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy pressed harder and harder; for three months the defenders never laid aside their armor, day or night.

sentences.zh: 太祖自將來援，圍始解，論功與克敵等。

translations.literal: The Founder personally led troops to relieve them, and the siege was at last lifted; when merit was reckoned he was graded equal to those credited with defeating the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder came in person to relieve the city, and the siege was finally broken; when rewards were distributed, Yu received credit on par with the chief victors.

sentences.zh: 太祖已平武昌，使愈帥兵徇江西未附州縣。

translations.literal: After the Founder had pacified Wuchang, he had Yu lead troops to reduce the unsubmitted prefectures and counties of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Founder had pacified Wuchang, he sent Yu to subdue the Jiangxi prefectures and counties still holding out.

sentences.zh: 鄧克明之弟志清據永豐，有卒二萬。

translations.literal: Deng Keming's younger brother Zhiqing held Yongfeng and had twenty thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Keming's younger brother Zhiqing held Yongfeng with twenty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 愈擊破之，擒其大帥五十餘人。

translations.literal: Yu routed him and captured more than fifty of his chief commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Yu smashed his force and captured more than fifty of his senior commanders.

sentences.zh: 從常遇春平沙坑、麻嶺諸寨，進兵取吉安，圍贛州，五月乃克之。

translations.literal: Following Chang Yuchun he pacified the stockades of Shakeng and Maling and the rest, advanced to take Ji'an, besieged Ganzhou, and only in the fifth month captured it.
translations.idiomatic: With Chang Yuchun he pacified the stockades at Shakeng, Maling, and elsewhere, marched on Ji'an, besieged Ganzhou, and took it only after five months.

sentences.zh: 進江西行省右丞，時年二十八。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat; at the time he was twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat at the age of twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 兵興，諸將早貴未有如愈與李文忠者。

translations.literal: Since the rise of the armies, among the generals none had attained high rank so early as Yu and Li Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the founding wars, no general had risen to eminence as young as Yu and Li Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 愈為人簡重慎密，不憚危苦，將軍嚴，善撫降附。

translations.literal: Yu as a man was simple, grave, and discreet; he did not shrink from danger and hardship; in commanding troops he was strict, and he was skilled at comforting those who surrendered and submitted.
