translations.idiomatic: Yu was plain, grave, and discreet, unafraid of hardship; he commanded with strict discipline yet knew how to win over those who surrendered.

sentences.zh: 其徇安福也，部卒有虜掠者。

translations.literal: When he reduced Anfu, there were soldiers in his command who carried off plunder.
translations.idiomatic: During his subjugation of Anfu, some of his troops looted the populace.

sentences.zh: 判官潘樞入謁，面責之。

translations.literal: The judge Pan Shu entered to have an audience and rebuked him to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Judge Pan Shu came to see him and rebuked him to his face.

sentences.zh: 愈驚起謝，趣下令掠民者斬，索軍中所得子女盡出之。

translations.literal: Yu started up in alarm and apologized, urgently ordered that those who plundered the people be executed, and demanded that all women and children taken within the army be brought out.
translations.idiomatic: Yu rose in alarm and apologized, immediately ordered looters executed, and had every woman and child seized by his troops returned.

sentences.zh: 樞因閉置空舍中，自坐舍外，作糜食之。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon shut them in empty houses and himself sat outside the houses, preparing gruel to feed them.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Shu housed the victims in empty quarters, sat outside himself, and prepared gruel for them.

sentences.zh: 卒有謀乘夜劫取者，愈鞭之以徇。

translations.literal: When soldiers plotted to seize them by night, Yu had them flogged as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: When some soldiers plotted to seize the victims by night, Yu had them flogged as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 樞悉護遣還其家，民大悅。

translations.literal: Shu escorted them all and sent them back to their families; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Shu saw them all safely home, and the people were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 已而遇春克襄陽，以愈為湖廣行省平章鎮其地，賜以書曰：「爾戍襄陽，宜謹守法度。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Yuchun captured Xiangyang; Yu was made Pacification Commissioner of the Huguang Branch Secretariat to garrison the region, and was granted a letter saying: "You garrison Xiangyang and ought carefully to observe law and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chang Yuchun took Xiangyang, and Yu was made Pacification Commissioner of the Huguang Branch Secretariat to hold the region. The Founder wrote him: "As you garrison Xiangyang, you must strictly uphold the law.

sentences.zh: 山寨來歸者，兵民悉仍故籍，小校以下悉令屯種，且耕且戰。

translations.literal: Those who come from mountain stockades to submit—soldiers and civilians alike shall remain on their former registers; all below company commanders shall be ordered to garrison and farm, fighting even as they plow.
translations.idiomatic: For stockade people who submit, soldiers and civilians alike shall keep their old registers; all ranks below company commander shall farm garrison lands, fighting even as they plow.

sentences.zh: 爾所戍地鄰擴廓，若爾愛加於民，法行於軍，則彼所部皆將慕義來歸，如脫虎口就慈母。

translations.literal: The place you garrison adjoins Köke Temür; if you extend love to the people and enforce law in the army, then those under him will all admire righteousness and come to submit, as if escaping a tiger's maw to reach a loving mother.
translations.idiomatic: Your post borders Köke Temür's domain. If you show the people kindness and enforce discipline in the army, his followers will come over in admiration of your righteousness, as though escaping a tiger's jaws to find a mother's embrace.

sentences.zh: 我賴爾如長城，爾其勉之！」

translations.literal: I rely on you as on the Long Wall— exert yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: I depend on you as on the Great Wall— do your utmost!"

sentences.zh: 愈披荊棘，立軍府營屯，拊循招徠，威惠甚著。

translations.literal: Yu cleared brambles, established military offices and garrison colonies, soothed and summoned people, and his authority and kindness were greatly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Yu cleared the wilderness, established headquarters and garrison farms, and won people through kindness and firm rule; his reputation for justice and benevolence spread far.

sentences.zh: 吳元年建御史台，召為右御史大夫，領台事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wu the Censorate was established; he was summoned as Right Censor-in-Chief to head its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Wu regime the Censorate was established, and he was summoned as Right Censor-in-Chief to head it.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年兼太子諭德。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu he concurrently served as Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 he also served as Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 大軍經略中原，愈為征戍將軍，帥襄、漢兵取南陽以北未附州郡。

translations.literal: As the great army planned its advance into the Central Plains, Yu served as Expeditionary Garrison General, leading the Xiang and Han troops to take the unsubmitted prefectures north of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: As the main army advanced into the Central Plains, Yu served as Expeditionary Garrison General, leading Xiang and Han forces to seize the prefectures north of Nanyang still holding out.

sentences.zh: 遂克唐州，進攻南陽，敗元兵於瓦店，逐北抵城下，遂克之，擒史國公等二十六人。

translations.literal: He thereupon captured Tangzhou, advanced to attack Nanyang, defeated Yuan troops at Wadian, pursued north to the foot of the walls, and thereby captured it, seizing Duke of State Shi and twenty-six others.
translations.idiomatic: He took Tangzhou, advanced on Nanyang, routed Yuan forces at Wadian, pursued them to the city walls, and captured the city, seizing Duke of State Shi and twenty-six others.

sentences.zh: 隋、葉、舞陽、魯山諸州縣相繼降。

translations.literal: The prefectures and counties of Sui, Ye, Wuyang, Lushan, and the rest submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Sui, Ye, Wuyang, Lushan, and neighboring prefectures and counties surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 攻下牛心、光石、洪山諸山寨，均、房、金、商之地悉定。

translations.literal: He attacked and took the mountain stockades of Niuxin, Guangshi, Hongshan, and the rest; the territories of Jun, Fang, Jin, and Shang were all settled.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced the stockades at Niuxin, Guangshi, Hongshan, and elsewhere, bringing the regions of Jun, Fang, Jin, and Shang fully under control.

sentences.zh: 三年，以征虜左副副將軍從大將軍出定西。

translations.literal: In the third year, as Left Associate Vice General of the Expeditionary Force against the Barbarians he followed the Grand General in marching out to pacify the west.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he served as Left Associate Vice General of the Expeditionary Force against the Barbarians and marched west with the Grand General.

sentences.zh: 擴廓屯車道峴，愈直抵其壘，立柵逼之，擴廓敗走。

translations.literal: Köke Temür encamped at Chedao Xian; Yu went straight to his camp, erected palisades to press him, and Köke Temür was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür encamped at Chedao Xian; Yu marched straight to his lines, threw up palisades to hem him in, and drove him off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 分兵自臨洮進克河州，招諭吐蕃諸酋長，宣慰何鎖南普等皆納印請降。

translations.literal: He divided his forces and advanced from Lintao to capture Hezhou, summoned and instructed the various chieftains of the Tibetans, and Pacification Commissioner He Suonanpu and others all surrendered their seals and requested submission.
translations.idiomatic: Detaching a force from Lintao, he took Hezhou and summoned the Tibetan chieftains; Pacification Commissioner He Suonanpu and others all surrendered their seals.

sentences.zh: 追豫王至西黃河，抵黑松林，破斬其大將。

translations.literal: He pursued the Prince of Henan to the Western Yellow River, reached Black Pine Forest, routed and beheaded his great general.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the Prince of Henan to the Western Yellow River, reached Black Pine Forest, and killed his chief general in battle.

sentences.zh: 河州以西朵甘、烏斯藏諸部悉歸附。

translations.literal: West of Hezhou the various tribes of Do-Kham and Ü-Tsang all submitted and attached themselves.
translations.idiomatic: All the Do-Kham and Ü-Tsang tribes west of Hezhou submitted.

sentences.zh: 出甘肅西北數千里而還。

translations.literal: He went out several thousand li into the northwest of Gansu and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He marched several thousand li into northwestern Gansu before returning.

sentences.zh: 論功授開國輔運推誠宣力武臣、特進榮祿大夫、右柱國，封衛國公，同參軍國事，歲祿三千石，予世券。

translations.literal: When merit was reckoned he was granted the titles Founding Merit Minister Who Assists the Dynasty, Promotes Sincerity, and Proclaims Strength in War, Special Advancement Grand Master of Glorious Blessings, and Right Pillar of the State; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Weiguo, given concurrent participation in state affairs, an income of three thousand piculs, and a hereditary patent of privilege.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he received the titles Founding Merit Minister Who Assists the Dynasty, Promotes Sincerity, and Proclaims Strength in War, Special Advancement Grand Master of Glorious Blessings, and Right Pillar of the State; he was enfeoffed Duke of Weiguo with a voice in state affairs, an income of three thousand piculs, and a hereditary patent of privilege.

sentences.zh: 四年伐蜀，命愈赴襄陽練軍馬，運糧給軍士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Shu was attacked, he was ordered to go to Xiangyang to drill troops and horses and transport grain to supply the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, during the campaign against Shu, he was ordered to Xiangyang to train troops and horses and supply the army with grain.

sentences.zh: 五年，辰、澧諸蠻作亂，以愈為征南將軍，江夏侯周德興、江陰侯吳良為副。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the various tribes of Chen and Li rebelled; Yu was made General of the Southern Expedition, with Marquis of Jiangxia Zhou Dexing and Marquis of Jiangyin Wu Liang as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when the Chen and Li tribes rebelled, Yu was made General of the Southern Expedition, with Marquis of Jiangxia Zhou Dexing and Marquis of Jiangyin Wu Liang as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 討之。

translations.literal: They were sent to suppress the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to put down the uprising.

sentences.zh: 愈帥楊璟、黃彬出澧州，克四十八洞，又捕斬房州反者。

translations.literal: Yu led Yang Jing and Huang Bin out from Lizhou, captured forty-eight cave settlements, and again captured and beheaded the rebels of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu led Yang Jing and Huang Bin from Lizhou, took forty-eight cave settlements, and captured and executed the rebels of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，以右副將軍從徐達巡西北邊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, as Right Vice General he followed Xu Da in patrolling the northwestern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as Right Vice General and joined Xu Da in patrolling the northwest frontier.

sentences.zh: 十年，吐番川藏為梗，剽貢使，愈以征西將軍偕副將軍沐英討之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Tibetan Sichuan-Tibet route became obstructed and tribute envoys were plundered; Yu, as General of the Western Expedition, together with Vice General Mu Ying, was sent to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when Tibetan bandits on the Sichuan-Tibet route harassed the frontier and robbed tribute envoys, Yu was made General of the Western Expedition and, with Vice General Mu Ying, sent to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 分兵為三道，窮追至昆侖山，俘斬萬計，獲馬牛羊十余萬，留兵戍諸要害乃還。

translations.literal: He divided his forces into three routes, pursued to the ends at Kunlun Mountain, captured and killed numbering in the tens of thousands, obtained more than a hundred thousand horses, cattle, and sheep, left troops to garrison the various strategic points, and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He split his force into three columns, pursued the enemy to Kunlun Mountain, killed and captured tens of thousands, took more than a hundred thousand horses, cattle, and sheep, garrisoned the key passes, and returned.

sentences.zh: 道病，至壽春卒，年四十一。

translations.literal: He fell ill on the road, reached Shouchun, and died at the age of forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill on the march, reached Shouchun, and died at forty-one.

sentences.zh: 追封甯河王，諡武順。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ninghe with the posthumous title Martial and Orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Ninghe with the posthumous name Wushun, Martial and Orderly.

sentences.zh: 長子鎮嗣，改封申國公，以征南副將軍平永新龍泉山寇。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zhen succeeded; the title was changed to Duke of Shen; as Vice General of the Southern Expedition he pacified the bandits of Longquan Mountain in Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zhen succeeded him; the title was changed to Duke of Shen, and as Vice General of the Southern Expedition he pacified the bandits of Longquan Mountain in Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 再出塞，有功。

translations.literal: He again went beyond the frontier passes and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned beyond the frontier again with distinction.

sentences.zh: 其妻，李善長外孫也，善長敗，坐奸黨誅。

translations.literal: His wife was a granddaughter by marriage of Li Shanchang; when Shanchang fell, she was executed as a member of the treacherous faction.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was Li Shanchang's granddaughter by marriage; when Shanchang fell, she was executed as an accomplice in the treasonous faction.

sentences.zh: 弟銘錦衣衛指揮僉事，征蠻，卒於軍。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ming was Assistant Commander of the Brocade Guard; on the campaign against the tribes he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ming served as Assistant Commander of the Brocade Guard; he died on campaign against the tribes.

sentences.zh: 有子源為鎮後。

translations.literal: He had a son named Yuan who succeeded Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan inherited the title after Zhen.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，授源孫炳為南京錦衣衛世指揮使。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi reign Yuan's grandson Bing was appointed hereditary Commander of the Nanjing Brocade Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Hongzhi, Yuan's grandson Bing was made hereditary Commander of the Nanjing Brocade Guard.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年詔封炳子繼坤定遠侯。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiajing an edict enfeoffed Bing's son Jikun as Marquis of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 11 an edict enfeoffed Bing's son Jikun as Marquis of Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 五傳至文明，崇禎末，死流賊之難。

translations.literal: After five generations it reached Wenming; at the end of Chongzhen he died in the calamity of the roving bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed five generations to Wenming, who perished in the rebel turmoil at the end of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 湯和，字鼎臣，濠人，與太祖同里閈。

translations.literal: Tang He, courtesy name Dingchen, was a native of Hao and shared the same lane with the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: Tang He, courtesy name Dingchen, came from Hao and grew up in the same neighborhood as the Founder.

sentences.zh: 幼有奇志，嬉戲嘗習騎射，部勒群兒。

translations.literal: From youth he had an extraordinary will; in play he would practice riding and archery and drill the band of boys.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he showed unusual ambition, practicing riding and archery in play and drilling the other children.

sentences.zh: 及長，身長七尺，倜儻多計略。

translations.literal: When he grew up he stood seven chi in height, was free and easy in manner, and possessed many stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood, he stood seven chi tall, carried himself with easy boldness, and was full of stratagems.

sentences.zh: 郭子興初起，和帥壯士十余人歸之，以功授千戶。

translations.literal: When Guo Zixing first rose, He led more than ten stalwart men to join him and, for merit, was appointed commander of a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Zixing first raised his banner, He brought more than ten stalwart followers to join him and, for his service, was made commander of a thousand.

sentences.zh: 從太祖攻大洪山，克滁州，授管軍總管。

translations.literal: He followed the Founder in attacking Dahong Mountain, captured Chuzhou, and was appointed Military Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Founder in the assault on Dahong Mountain, helped take Chuzhou, and was made Military Commandant.

sentences.zh: 從取和州。

translations.literal: He followed in taking Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He joined in the capture of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 時諸將多太祖等夷，莫肯為下。

translations.literal: At the time many of the generals considered themselves the Founder's equals and were unwilling to serve beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many generals regarded themselves as the Founder's equals and refused to submit to him.

sentences.zh: 和長太祖三歲，獨奉約束甚謹，太祖甚悅之。

translations.literal: He was three years older than the Founder, yet alone observed discipline with great strictness; the Founder was greatly pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Though three years older than the Founder, he alone submitted to discipline with scrupulous loyalty, and the Founder was deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 從定太平，獲馬三百。

translations.literal: He followed in settling Taiping and obtained three hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Taiping and captured three hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 從擊陳野先，流矢中左股，拔矢復鬥，卒與諸將破擒野先。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Chen Yexian; a stray arrow struck his left thigh, he pulled out the arrow and fought again, and in the end together with the generals routed and captured Yexian.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Chen Yexian a stray arrow struck his left thigh; he pulled it out and kept fighting, and in the end he and the other generals routed and captured Yexian.

sentences.zh: 別下溧水、句容，從定集慶。

translations.literal: On separate campaigns he took Lishui and Jurong, and followed in settling Jiqing.
translations.idiomatic: On separate operations he took Lishui and Jurong, then joined in the pacification of Jiqing.

sentences.zh: 從徐達取鎮江，進統軍元師。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da in taking Zhenjiang and was promoted to Marshal of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Xu Da in capturing Zhenjiang and was promoted to Marshal of the Army.

sentences.zh: 徇奔牛、呂城，降陳保二。

translations.literal: He marched to reduce Beniu and Lücheng and accepted the surrender of Chen Bao'er.
translations.idiomatic: He subdued Beniu and Lücheng and received the surrender of Chen Bao'er.

sentences.zh: 取金壇、常州，以和為樞密院同僉守之。

translations.literal: He took Jintan and Changzhou, and He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: Jintan and Changzhou were captured, and Tang He was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs to hold them.

sentences.zh: 常與吳接境，張士誠間諜百出，和防禦嚴密，敵莫能窺。

translations.literal: Changzhou bordered Wu territory; Zhang Shicheng's spies appeared everywhere; He's defenses were strict and tight, and the enemy could not spy them out.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou lay on the border with Wu, and Zhang Shicheng sent spies in every direction, but He's defenses were so tight that the enemy could find no opening.

sentences.zh: 再寇，再擊卻之，俘斬千計。

translations.literal: They raided again; he repelled them again; captives taken and heads cut off numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When they raided again, he drove them back again, and prisoners and slain enemies numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 進攻無錫，大破吳軍於錫山，走莫天祐，獲其妻子，進中書左丞。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Wuxi, he routed the Wu army at Xishan, drove off Mo Tianyou, captured his wife and children, and was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Wuxi and shattered the Wu army at Xishan, putting Mo Tianyou to flight and taking his wife and children captive; for this he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以舟師徇黃楊山，敗吳水軍，獲千戶四十九人，拜平章政事。

translations.literal: With a fleet he marched on Huangyang Mountain, defeated the Wu navy, captured forty-nine commanders of a thousand, and was appointed Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Leading a fleet against Huangyang Mountain, he crushed the Wu navy, took forty-nine thousand-household commanders prisoner, and was made Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 援長興，與張士信戰城下。

translations.literal: He went to relieve Changxing and fought Zhang Shixin beneath the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to relieve Changxing and battled Zhang Shixin under the city walls.

sentences.zh: 城中兵出夾擊，大敗之，俘卒八千，解圍而還。

translations.literal: Troops from the city came out in a pincer attack; he routed them utterly, took eight thousand prisoners, lifted the siege, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When garrison troops sallied out in a pincer attack, he routed them completely, took eight thousand prisoners, broke the siege, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 討平江西諸山寨。

translations.literal: He campaigned and pacified the mountain strongholds of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He subdued the mountain strongholds throughout Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 永新守將周安叛，進擊敗之，連破其十七寨，圍城三月，克之，執安以獻，還守常州。

translations.literal: Zhou An, garrison commander of Yongxin, rebelled; he advanced, defeated him, broke seventeen stockades in succession, besieged the city for three months, took it, seized An and presented him as a captive, then returned to garrison Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou An, the Yongxin garrison commander, rebelled, he advanced, defeated him, stormed seventeen stockades in a row, and after a three-month siege took the city, seized Zhou An and sent him up as a captive, then returned to hold Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 從大軍伐士誠，克太湖水寨，下吳江州，圍平江，戰於閶門，飛礮傷左臂，召還應天，創愈復往，攻克之，論功賜金帛。

translations.literal: Following the grand army in the campaign against Shicheng, he captured the Taihu water fort, took Wujiang Prefecture, besieged Pingjiang, fought at Chang Gate; a flying bomb wounded his left arm; he was recalled to Yingtian; when his wound healed he returned, stormed and took the city, and for merit was rewarded with gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the main army against Zhang Shicheng, took the Taihu water fort and Wujiang Prefecture, and besieged Pingjiang. At Chang Gate a flying bomb wounded his left arm; recalled to Yingtian, he returned once healed, captured the city, and was rewarded with gold and silk for his service.

sentences.zh: 大軍方北伐，命造舟明州，運糧輸直沽。

translations.literal: While the grand army was advancing north, he was ordered to build ships at Mingzhou and transport grain to Zhigu.
translations.idiomatic: While the main army marched north, he was ordered to build ships at Mingzhou and carry grain to Zhigu.

sentences.zh: 海多颶風，輸鎮江而還。

translations.literal: Hurricanes were frequent at sea; he delivered the grain to Zhenjiang and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Storms were frequent at sea, so he delivered the grain as far as Zhenjiang and turned back.

sentences.zh: 拜偏將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice General.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice General.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍西征，與右副將軍馮勝自懷慶逾太行，取澤、潞、晉、絳諸州郡。

translations.literal: Following the Grand General on the western campaign, he and Right Vice General Feng Sheng crossed the Taihang from Huaqing and took the prefectures and commanderies of Ze, Lu, Jin, and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: On the western campaign under the Grand General, he and Right Vice General Feng Sheng crossed the Taihang from Huaqing and captured Ze, Lu, Jin, Jiang, and the other prefectures and commanderies there.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍拔河中。

translations.literal: He followed the Grand General in taking Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Grand General in capturing Hedong.

sentences.zh: 明年，渡河入潼關，分兵趨涇州，使部將招降張良臣，既而叛去。

translations.literal: The next year he crossed the river and entered Tong Pass, sent a detachment toward Jingzhou, and had a subordinate general induce Zhang Liangchen to surrender; Liangchen soon rebelled and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he crossed the river into Tong Pass, dispatched a detachment toward Jingzhou, and had a subordinate induce Zhang Liangchen to surrender, but Liangchen soon rebelled and broke away.

sentences.zh: 會大軍圍慶陽，執斬之。

translations.literal: When the grand army besieged Qingyang, they captured and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army besieged Qingyang, he was captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 又明年，復以右副副將軍從大將軍敗擴廓於定西，遂定寧夏，逐北至察罕腦兒，擒猛將虎陳，獲馬牛羊十余萬。

translations.literal: The year after that, again as Right Vice Vice General he followed the Grand General in defeating Köke Temür at Dingxi, then settled Ningxia, pursued north to Chaghan-naur, captured the fierce general Hu Chen, and obtained more than a hundred thousand horses, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, again serving as Right Vice Vice General under the Grand General, he defeated Köke Temür at Dingxi, pacified Ningxia, pursued the enemy north to Chaghan-naur, captured the fierce general Hu Chen, and seized more than a hundred thousand horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 徇東勝、大同、宣府皆有功。

translations.literal: In campaigns against Dongsheng, Datong, and Xuanfu he won merit each time.
translations.idiomatic: On campaigns through Dongsheng, Datong, and Xuanfu he distinguished himself each time.

sentences.zh: 還，授開國輔運推誠宣力武臣、榮祿大夫、柱國，封中山侯，歲祿千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: On his return he was granted the titles Founding Martial Minister Who Aids the Dynasty with Sincere Merit, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Pillar of the State; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhongshan with an annual stipend of fifteen hundred shi, and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he received the titles Founding Martial Minister Who Aids the Dynasty with Sincere Merit, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Pillar of the State; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhongshan with a stipend of fifteen hundred shi and given a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 四年拜征西將軍，與副將軍廖永忠帥舟師溯江伐夏。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed General Who Conquers the West; with Vice General Liao Yongzhong he led a fleet upriver to attack Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made General Who Conquers the West and, with Vice General Liao Yongzhong, led a fleet up the Yangzi to attack Xia.

sentences.zh: 夏人以兵扼險，攻不克。

translations.literal: The Xia troops blocked the strategic passes with their forces; the attack could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Xia forces held the mountain passes, and the assault failed.

sentences.zh: 江水暴漲，駐師大溪口，久不進，而傅友德已自秦、隴深入，取漢中。

translations.literal: The river swelled suddenly; the army halted at Daxi Pass and did not advance for a long time, while Fu Youde had already advanced deep from Qin and Long and taken Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The river rose in flood, and the army lingered at Daxi Pass without advancing for a long time, even as Fu Youde had already pushed deep from Qin and Long and taken Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 永忠先驅破瞿塘關，入夔州。

translations.literal: Yongzhong as vanguard broke through Qutang Pass and entered Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong led the vanguard through Qutang Pass and into Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 和乃引軍繼之，入重慶，降明升。

translations.literal: He then led his army after him, entered Chongqing, and received the surrender of Ming Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought his army up after him, entered Chongqing, and accepted the surrender of Ming Sheng.

sentences.zh: 師還，友德、永忠受上賞，而和不及。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Youde and Yongzhong received the highest rewards, but He did not share in them.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Youde and Yongzhong received the highest honors, but He was passed over.

sentences.zh: 明年從大將軍北伐，遇敵於斷頭山，戰敗，亡一指揮，帝不問。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the Grand General on the northern campaign; they met the enemy at Duan Tou Mountain, were defeated, and lost one commander; the Emperor did not hold him to account.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he joined the Grand General's northern campaign; at Duan Tou Mountain they met the enemy, were defeated, and lost a commander, yet the Emperor did not reproach him.

sentences.zh: 尋與李善長營中都宮闕。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he joined Li Shanchang in building the palace complex at the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he joined Li Shanchang in constructing the palace at the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 鎮北平，甓彰德城。

translations.literal: He garrisoned Beiping and bricked the walls of Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Beiping and rebuilt the walls of Zhangde with brick.

sentences.zh: 征察罕腦兒，大捷。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Chaghan-naur he won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Chaghan-naur he scored a great victory.

sentences.zh: 九年，伯顏帖木兒為邊患，以征西將軍防延安。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Boyan Temür troubled the frontier; as General Who Conquers the West he defended Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, with Boyan Temür raiding the frontier, he served as General Who Conquers the West and defended Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 伯顏乞和，乃還。

translations.literal: Boyan sued for peace, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Boyan sued for peace, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，進封信國公，歲祿三千石，議軍國事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year he was advanced to Duke of Xin with an annual stipend of three thousand shi and consulted on military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year he was promoted to Duke of Xin with a stipend of three thousand shi and given a voice in deliberations on military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 數出中都、臨清、北平練軍伍，完城郭。

translations.literal: He went out repeatedly to the Central Capital, Linqing, and Beiping to drill troops and complete city defenses.
translations.idiomatic: He went out again and again to the Central Capital, Linqing, and Beiping to drill troops and finish the city defenses.

sentences.zh: 十四年以左副將軍出塞，征乃兒不花，破敵灰山營，獲平章別裏哥、樞密使久通而還。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, as Left Vice General he went beyond the passes to campaign against Nayirbuqa, broke the enemy's camp at Mount Hui, captured the Grand Councillor Berke and the Bureau Commissioner of Military Affairs Jiutong, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he crossed the frontier as Left Vice General to campaign against Nayirbuqa, smashed the enemy camp at Mount Hui, captured Grand Councillor Berke and Bureau Commissioner Jiutong, and returned.

sentences.zh: 十八年，思州蠻叛，以征虜將軍從楚王討平之，俘獲四萬，擒其酋以歸。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Si prefecture tribes rebelled; as General Who Subdues Barbarians he followed the Prince of Chu to pacify them, took forty thousand captives, and brought back their chieftain as a prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, when the Si tribes rebelled, he served as General Who Subdues Barbarians under the Prince of Chu, pacified them, took forty thousand captives, and brought back their chieftain in chains.

sentences.zh: 和沉敏多智數，頗有酒過。

translations.literal: He was deep, quick-witted, and full of stratagems, though he had a weakness for drink.
translations.idiomatic: He was shrewd and resourceful, though he had a weakness for wine.

sentences.zh: 守常州時，嘗請事于太祖，不得，醉出怨言曰：「吾鎮此城，如坐屋脊，左顧則左，右顧則右。」

translations.literal: While garrisoning Changzhou he once requested an audience with the Founder and was refused; drunk, he went out muttering, "I hold this city like sitting on a roof ridge—look left and I go left, look right and I go right.
translations.idiomatic: While holding Changzhou he once asked to see the Founder and was refused; drunk, he went out grumbling, "I hold this city as one sits on a roof ridge—look left and I turn left, look right and I turn right.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞而銜之。

translations.literal: The Founder heard of it and bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder heard of this and never forgot it.

sentences.zh: 平中原師還論功，以和征閩時放遣陳友定餘孽，八郡復擾，師還，為秀蘭山賊所襲，失二指揮，故不得封公。

translations.literal: When the army that pacified the Central Plains returned and merits were weighed, because during He's campaign in Min he had released the remnants of Chen Youding's forces, eight prefectures were disturbed again, and on the army's return he was ambushed by bandits at Xiulan Mountain and lost two commanders; for this he was not enfeoffed as duke.
translations.idiomatic: When merits were weighed after the Central Plains campaign, he was denied a ducal title because during his Min campaign he had released Chen Youding's remaining followers, eight prefectures were thrown into turmoil again, and on the march home his force was ambushed at Xiulan Mountain and lost two commanders.

sentences.zh: 伐蜀還，面數其逗撓罪。

translations.literal: On returning from the Shu campaign, the Emperor confronted him and enumerated his crimes of delay and slackness.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from the Shu campaign, the Emperor confronted him face to face and listed his crimes of delay and slackness.

sentences.zh: 頓首謝，乃已。

translations.literal: He kowtowed in apology, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed in apology, and the Emperor let the matter rest.

sentences.zh: 其封信國公也，猶數其常州時過失，鐫之券。

translations.literal: Even when he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xin, his past faults at Changzhou were still recounted and inscribed on the patent.
translations.idiomatic: Even when he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xin, his old misconduct at Changzhou was still recounted and carved into the patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 于時，帝春秋浸高，天下無事，魏國、曹國皆前卒，意不欲諸將久典兵，未有以發也。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor's years were advancing, the realm was at peace, the Dukes of Wei and Cao had both died earlier, and he wished not to leave generals long in command of armies, yet had no occasion to act.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Emperor was growing old, the realm was at peace, and the Dukes of Wei and Cao had already died; he wanted no general to hold command too long, but had found no occasion to act.

sentences.zh: 和以間從容言：「臣犬馬齒長，不堪復任驅策，願得歸故鄉，為容棺之墟，以待骸骨。」

translations.literal: He seized an occasion to say gently, "Your servant's dog-and-horse years have grown long; I can no longer bear to be driven in service. I wish to return to my native place and make a plot to hold my coffin, there to await my bones.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing a suitable moment, he said gently, "Your servant's years have grown long; I can no longer bear to be driven in your service. I wish to return home and prepare a place for my coffin, there to await my bones.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，立賜鈔治第中都，並為諸公、侯治第。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased, immediately granted paper money for a residence at the Central Capital, and had mansions built for the other dukes and marquises as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted, immediately granted paper money for a mansion at the Central Capital, and had residences built for the other dukes and marquises as well.

sentences.zh: 既而倭寇上海，帝患之，顧謂和曰：「卿雖老，強為朕一行。」

translations.literal: Before long Japanese pirates raided Shanghai; the Emperor was troubled by it and, turning to He, said, "Though you are old, do this one thing for me.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Japanese pirates struck Shanghai; troubled by this, the Emperor turned to He and said, "Though you are old, do this one service for me.

sentences.zh: 和請與方鳴謙俱。

translations.literal: He requested to go together with Fang Mingqian.
translations.idiomatic: He asked permission to take Fang Mingqian with him.

sentences.zh: 鳴謙，國珍從子也，習海事，常訪以禦倭策。

translations.literal: Mingqian was a nephew of Fang Guozhen, versed in maritime affairs; the Emperor often consulted him on strategies against the Japanese pirates.
translations.idiomatic: Mingqian was a nephew of Fang Guozhen and knew maritime affairs well; the Emperor often consulted him on how to repel the pirates.

sentences.zh: 鳴謙曰：「倭海上來，則海上御之耳。

translations.literal: Mingqian said, "When the Japanese come by sea, they should be met at sea.
translations.idiomatic: Mingqian said, "When the Japanese come from the sea, they must be met on the sea.

sentences.zh: 請量地遠近，置衛所，陸聚步兵，水具戰艦，則倭不得入，入亦不得傅岸。

translations.literal: Measure the distances along the coast, establish guard stations, mass infantry on land and equip warships on the water—then the Japanese cannot enter, and if they enter they cannot reach shore.
translations.idiomatic: Measure the distances along the coast, establish guard stations, mass infantry on land and ready warships on the water, and the Japanese will neither enter nor, if they enter, reach the shore.

sentences.zh: 近海民四丁籍一以為軍，戍守之，可無煩客兵也。」

translations.literal: Register one man in four from coastal households for military service to garrison the defenses, and there will be no need to trouble outside troops.
translations.idiomatic: Draft one man in four from coastal households for garrison duty, and there will be no need to rely on outside troops.

sentences.zh: 帝以為然。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed that this was sound.

sentences.zh: 和乃度地浙西東，並海設衛所城五十有九，選丁壯三萬五千人築之，盡發州縣錢及籍罪人貲給役。

translations.literal: He then surveyed the land in western and eastern Zhejiang, established fifty-nine guard-station fortresses along the coast, selected thirty-five thousand strong young men to build them, and spent all the funds of prefectures and counties plus the registered assets of convicts to pay for the labor.
translations.idiomatic: He then surveyed western and eastern Zhejiang, built fifty-nine coastal guard-station fortresses, drafted thirty-five thousand strong young men to construct them, and spent every penny from the prefectures and counties plus the registered property of convicts to pay for the work.

sentences.zh: 役夫往往過望，而民不能無擾，浙人頗苦之。

translations.literal: The corvée workers often exceeded their allotted quotas, yet the people could not be free of disturbance; the people of Zhejiang suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Labor quotas were often exceeded, yet the people could not escape hardship, and the people of Zhejiang suffered sorely.

sentences.zh: 或謂和曰：「民讟矣，奈何？」

translations.literal: Someone said to He, "The people are cursing you—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to him, "The people are cursing you—what will you do?

sentences.zh: 和曰：「成遠算者不恤近怨，任大事者不顧細謹，復有讟者，齒吾劍。」

translations.literal: He said, "One who achieves a far-reaching plan does not fret over near resentments; one entrusted with great affairs does not fuss over small proprieties. If anyone curses again, let him taste my sword."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "One who plans for the long term does not worry about present resentment; one charged with great affairs does not fuss over small niceties. If anyone curses again, let him taste my sword."

sentences.zh: 逾年而城成。

translations.literal: Within a year the fortresses were completed.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year the fortifications were finished.

sentences.zh: 稽軍次，定考格，立賞令。

translations.literal: He inspected military ranks, fixed standards for evaluation, and established reward ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed military ranks, set standards for evaluation, and issued reward regulations.

sentences.zh: 浙東民四丁以上者，戶取一丁戍之，凡得五萬八千七百餘人。

translations.literal: From households in eastern Zhejiang with four or more adult males, one man per household was taken for garrison duty; in all fifty-eight thousand seven hundred-odd men were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: From households in eastern Zhejiang with four adult males or more, one man per household was drafted for garrison duty, yielding fifty-eight thousand seven hundred-odd men in all.

sentences.zh: 明年，閩中並海城工竣，和還報命，中都新第亦成。

translations.literal: The next year the coastal fortifications in Min were finished as well; He returned to report his mission, and his new mansion at the Central Capital was also completed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the coastal fortifications in Min were finished as well; he returned to report completion of his mission, and his new mansion at the Central Capital was also ready.

sentences.zh: 和帥妻子陛辭，賜黃金三百兩、白金二千兩、鈔三千錠、彩幣四十有副，夫人胡氏賜亦稱是。

translations.literal: He brought his wife and children to take leave at court; he was granted three hundred taels of gold, two thousand taels of silver, three thousand ingots of paper money, and forty pairs of brocade bolts; his wife Lady Hu received the same.
translations.idiomatic: He brought his wife and children to court to take leave; he was granted three hundred taels of gold, two thousand taels of silver, three thousand ingots of paper money, and forty pairs of brocade bolts, and Lady Hu received the same.

sentences.zh: 並降璽書褒諭，諸功臣莫得比焉。

translations.literal: An imperial patent of praise was also sent down; none of the other meritorious ministers could compare.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial patent of praise was also issued, and none of the other meritorious ministers could compare with him.

sentences.zh: 自是和歲一朝京師。

translations.literal: From then on He came once each year to pay court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he came to the capital once each year to pay court.

sentences.zh: 二十三年朝正旦，感疾失音。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he came for the New Year's audience and fell ill, losing his voice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he came for the New Year's audience, fell ill, and lost his voice.

sentences.zh: 帝即日臨視，惋歎久之，遣還裏。

translations.literal: The Emperor that same day came in person to visit him, sighed long in regret, and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the Emperor came in person to see him, sighed long in sorrow, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 疾小間，復命其子迎至都，俾以安車入內殿，宴勞備至，賜金帛禦膳法酒相屬。

translations.literal: When his illness eased somewhat, he again had his son bring him to the capital, had him enter the inner hall in a comfortable carriage, entertained and rewarded him with every courtesy, and granted gold, silk, imperial meals, and ceremonial wine in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness eased, the Emperor again had his son bring him to the capital, received him in the inner hall in a comfortable carriage, entertained him with every honor, and showered him with gold, silk, imperial meals, and ceremonial wine.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，病浸篤不能興。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year his illness grew grave and he could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year his illness worsened until he could no longer rise.

sentences.zh: 帝思見之，詔以安車入覲，手拊摩之，與敘裏閈故舊及兵興艱難事甚悉。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to see him and ordered him brought in a comfortable carriage for an audience; he stroked him with his own hand and spoke at length of old neighbors and friends and of the hardships when the army first rose.
translations.idiomatic: Longing to see him, the Emperor ordered him brought to court in a comfortable carriage, stroked him with his own hand, and spoke at length of old neighbors, old friends, and the hardships of the founding wars.

sentences.zh: 和不能對，稽首而已。

translations.literal: He could not reply and could only kowtow.
translations.idiomatic: He could not answer and could only kowtow.

sentences.zh: 帝為流涕，厚賜金帛為葬費。

translations.literal: The Emperor wept for him and richly granted gold and silk for his burial expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wept for him and generously granted gold and silk for his burial.

sentences.zh: 明年八月卒，年七十，追封東甌王，諡襄武。

translations.literal: The next year, in the eighth month, he died at the age of seventy; he was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Dong'ou with the posthumous title Xiangwu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the eighth month, he died at seventy; he was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Dong'ou with the posthumous title Xiangwu.

sentences.zh: 和晚年益為恭慎，入聞國論，一語不敢外泄。

translations.literal: In his later years He grew ever more deferential and cautious; when he heard state deliberations, not a word would he let slip outside.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he grew ever more deferential and cautious; when he heard state deliberations, he never let a word slip outside.

sentences.zh: 媵妾百餘，病後悉資遣之。

translations.literal: He had more than a hundred secondary wives and concubines; after his illness he supplied funds and dismissed them all.
translations.idiomatic: He kept more than a hundred concubines; after his illness he settled them all and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 所得賞賜，多分遺鄉曲，見布衣時故交遺老，歡如也。

translations.literal: Most of what he received in rewards he distributed to neighbors in his home district; when he met old friends and elders from his days in plain cloth, he was as warm as ever.
translations.idiomatic: Most of what he received in rewards he gave away to neighbors at home, and when he met old friends and elders from his days in plain cloth, he was as warm as ever.

sentences.zh: 當時公、侯諸宿將坐奸党，先後麗法，稀得免者，而和獨享壽考，以功名終。

translations.literal: At that time the old generals who were dukes and marquises, implicated in factional crimes, one after another suffered capital punishment and few escaped; He alone enjoyed long life and ended his days in honor and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the old generals who were dukes and marquises, caught up in factional crimes, were one after another executed, and few escaped; He alone lived out a long life and ended his days in honor.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖間，東南苦倭患，和所築沿海城戍，皆堅緻，久且不圮，浙人賴以自保，多歌思之。

translations.literal: During the Jiajing reign the southeast suffered sorely from Japanese piracy; the coastal fortresses He had built were all solid and tight, enduring long without crumbling; the people of Zhejiang relied on them for self-defense and many sang his praises in remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign the southeast suffered greatly from Japanese piracy; the coastal fortresses He had built were solid and tight, enduring for years without crumbling, and the people of Zhejiang relied on them to defend themselves and sang his praises in remembrance.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史請於朝，立廟以祀。

translations.literal: The touring censor memorialized the court to establish a temple in his honor.
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor memorialized the court, and a temple was established in his honor.

sentences.zh: 和五子。

translations.literal: He had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Tang He had five sons.

sentences.zh: 長子鼎為前軍都督僉事，從征雲南，道卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ding was Vice Commissioner of the Vanguard Army; he followed a campaign to Yunnan and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ding served as Vice Commissioner of the Vanguard Army; he joined the Yunnan campaign and died on the march.

sentences.zh: 少子醴，積功至左軍都督同知，征五開，卒於軍。

translations.literal: His youngest son Li rose through merit to Left Vice Commissioner of the Army; on a campaign to Wukai he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Li rose through merit to Left Vice Commissioner of the Army; on a campaign to Wukai he died in service.

sentences.zh: 鼎子晟，晟子文瑜，皆早世，不得嗣。

translations.literal: Ding's son Sheng and Sheng's son Wenyü both died young and could not inherit.
translations.idiomatic: Ding's son Sheng and Sheng's son Wenyü both died young, so the line could not pass down.

sentences.zh: 英宗時，文瑜子傑乞嗣爵，竟以曆四十餘年未襲，罷之。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Yingzong, Wenyü's son Jie petitioned to inherit the title, but because more than forty years had passed without investiture, it was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Yingzong, Wenyü's son Jie petitioned to inherit the title, but because more than forty years had passed without succession, the claim was denied.

sentences.zh: 傑無子，以弟倫之子紹宗為後。

translations.literal: Jie had no son; he took his brother Lun's son Shaozong as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Jie had no son and adopted his brother Lun's son Shaozong as his heir.

sentences.zh: 孝宗錄功臣後，授紹宗南京錦衣衛世指揮使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong recorded the descendants of meritorious ministers and appointed Shaozong hereditary commander of the Nanjing Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong enrolled descendants of meritorious ministers and made Shaozong hereditary commander of the Nanjing Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年封靈璧侯，食祿千石。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiajing he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Lingbi, with an income of a thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Jiajing reign he was made Marquis of Lingbi with a stipend of a thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 傳子至孫世隆，隆慶中協守南京，兼領後府，改提督漕運，曆四十餘年，以勞加太子太保，進少保。

translations.literal: The title passed to his son and then to his grandson Shilong; during the Longqing reign Shilong assisted in the defense of Nanjing, concurrently headed the Rear Military Commission, was transferred to supervise grain transport on the Grand Canal, served more than forty years, and for his labors was promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and then Junior Mentor of the State.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed to his son and then to his grandson Shilong; during the Longqing reign Shilong helped defend Nanjing, concurrently headed the Rear Military Commission, was transferred to supervise grain transport on the Grand Canal, served more than forty years, and for his service was promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and then Junior Mentor of the State.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡僖敏。

translations.literal: He died and received the posthumous title Ximin.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously titled Ximin.

sentences.zh: 傳爵至明亡乃絕。

translations.literal: The patent passed down until the Ming dynasty fell, and then ended.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed down until the fall of the Ming, and then ended.

sentences.zh: 和曾孫胤勣，字公讓。

translations.literal: Tang He's great-grandson was Yinji, courtesy name Gongrang.
translations.idiomatic: He's great-grandson Yinji, whose courtesy name was Gongrang.

sentences.zh: 為諸生，工詩，負才使氣。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate, skilled in poetry, proud of his talent and quick to take offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate, skilled in poetry, proud of his gifts and quick to take offense.

sentences.zh: 巡撫尚書周忱使作啟事，即席具數萬言。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Minister Zhou Chen had him compose a memorial report; on the spot he produced tens of thousands of words.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Minister Zhou Chen had him draft a memorial report, and on the spot he produced tens of thousands of words.

sentences.zh: 忱薦之朝。

translations.literal: Chen recommended him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chen recommended him to the court.

sentences.zh: 少保于謙召詢古今將略及兵事，胤勣應對如響。

translations.literal: Junior Mentor Yu Qian summoned him to inquire about military stratagems ancient and modern and matters of war; Yinji answered as swiftly as an echo.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Mentor Yu Qian summoned him to question him on military stratagems ancient and modern and on matters of war, and Yinji answered as swiftly as an echo.

sentences.zh: 累授錦衣千戶。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed commander of a thousand in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to commander of a thousand in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 偕中書舍人趙榮通問英宗於沙漠，脫脫不花問中朝事，慷慨酬答不少屈。

translations.literal: Together with Secretariat Drafting Officer Zhao Rong he went to the desert to visit Emperor Yingzong; Totoqon asked about affairs of the Central Court, and he answered boldly without yielding in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Secretariat Drafting Officer Zhao Rong he went to the desert to visit Emperor Yingzong; when Totoqon questioned him about affairs at court, he answered boldly without yielding.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，用尚書胡濙薦，署指揮僉事。

translations.literal: During the Jingtai reign, on the recommendation of Minister Hu Ying, he was appointed acting Vice Commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingtai reign, on Minister Hu Ying's recommendation, he was appointed acting Vice Commander.

sentences.zh: 天順中，錦衣偵事者摭胤勣舊事以聞，謫為民。

translations.literal: During the Tianshun reign, Embroidered Uniform Guard investigators dredged up Yinji's old affairs and reported them; he was demoted to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshun reign, Embroidered Uniform Guard investigators dredged up Yinji's old affairs and reported them, and he was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 成化初，復故官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chenghua reign he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chenghua reign he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 三年擢署都指揮僉事，為延綏東路參將，分守孤山堡。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to acting Vice Commander-in-Chief, made Regional Vice Commander on the Eastern Route of Yan-sui, and assigned to garrison Gushan Fort separately.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to acting Vice Commander-in-Chief, appointed Regional Vice Commander on the Eastern Route of Yan-sui, and assigned to hold Gushan Fort.

sentences.zh: 孤山最當寇沖，胤勣奏請築城聚糧，增兵戍守。

translations.literal: Gushan lay most directly in the path of raiders; Yinji memorialized requesting to build walls, gather grain, and increase troops to garrison the post.
translations.idiomatic: Gushan stood squarely in the raiders' path; Yinji memorialized asking to fortify the place, stockpile grain, and reinforce the garrison.

sentences.zh: 未報，寇大至。

translations.literal: Before a reply came, the raiders arrived in force.
translations.idiomatic: Before any answer arrived, the enemy struck in overwhelming numbers.

sentences.zh: 胤勣病，力疾上馬，陷伏死。

translations.literal: Yinji was ill; forcing himself despite sickness he mounted his horse, fell into an ambush, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Though ill, Yinji dragged himself into the saddle, rode into an ambush, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈祭如例。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, he was granted posthumous honors and sacrifices according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned what had happened, he was granted the usual posthumous honors and sacrificial rites.

sentences.zh: 沐英，字文英，定遠人。

translations.literal: Mu Ying, courtesy name Wenying, was a native of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Ying, whose courtesy name was Wenying, came from Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 少孤，從母避兵，母又死。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he fled warfare with his mother; his mother then died.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father while still a boy and fled the fighting with his mother; she too soon died.

sentences.zh: 太祖與孝慈皇后憐之，撫為子，從硃姓。

translations.literal: The founding emperor and Empress Xiaoci took pity on him, raised him as a son, and he took the Zhu surname.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor and Empress Xiaoci took pity on the boy, adopted him as a son, and he took the Zhu surname.

sentences.zh: 年十八，授帳前都尉，守鎮江。

translations.literal: At eighteen he was appointed Captain of the Guard before the tent and put in charge of defending Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was made Captain of the Guard before the imperial tent and assigned to hold Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 稍遷指揮使，守廣信。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to commander and put in charge of defending Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to commander and posted to defend Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 已，從大軍征福建，破分水關，略崇安，別破閔溪十八寨，縛馮穀保。

translations.literal: Later he joined the main army on the Fujian campaign, broke through Fenshui Pass, overran Chong'an, separately broke eighteen stockades at Min Creek, and bound Feng Gubao.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined the main army on the Fujian campaign, stormed Fenshui Pass, overran Chong'an, separately reduced eighteen stockades along Min Creek, and captured Feng Gubao.

sentences.zh: 始命復姓。

translations.literal: Only then was he ordered to resume his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: Only then was he ordered to take back his original surname.

sentences.zh: 移鎮建甯，節制邵武、延平、汀州三衛。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command at Jianning, superintending the three garrisons of Shaowu, Yanping, and Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jianning, where he commanded the garrisons of Shaowu, Yanping, and Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋遷大都督府僉事，進同知。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Commissioner of the Chief Military Commission and promoted to Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Commissioner of the Chief Military Commission and then promoted to Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 府中機務繁積，英年少明敏，剖決無滯。

translations.literal: Official business at the commission piled up; though young, Ying was bright and quick, and his judgments never lagged.
translations.idiomatic: Business at the commission was heavy, but though still young Ying was sharp and quick, and his decisions never stalled.

sentences.zh: 後數稱其才，帝亦器重之。

translations.literal: Afterwards his talent was repeatedly praised, and the emperor also held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: His superiors soon began praising his talent again and again, and the emperor came to rely on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 洪武九年命乘傳詣關、陝，抵熙河，問民疾苦，事有不便，更置以聞。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongwu he was ordered to travel by relay post to the passes and Shaanxi, reaching the Xihé region, to inquire into the people's hardships; where matters were burdensome he changed arrangements and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Hongwu he was sent by relay post to the frontier passes and Shaanxi, as far as the Xihé region, to inquire into the people's hardships; wherever he found burdensome arrangements he revised them and reported back to the throne.

sentences.zh: 明年充征西副將軍，從衛國公鄧愈討吐番，西略川、藏，耀兵昆侖。

translations.literal: The next year he served as Vice General on the Western Expedition, following Duke of Weiguo Deng Yu against the Tibetans, extending westward into Sichuan and Tibet and displaying military might at Kunlun.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he served as vice general on the western expedition, following Duke of Weiguo Deng Yu against the Tibetans, pushing west into Sichuan and Tibet and parading his forces at Kunlun.

sentences.zh: 功多，封開國輔運推誠宣力武臣、榮祿大夫、柱國、西平侯，食祿二千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: For his many achievements he was enfeoffed as a meritorious founding minister who supports the state, promotes sincerity, and declares martial service, with the titles Grand Master for Glorious Emolument and Pillar of the State, made Marquis of Xiping with a stipend of 2,500 shi, and granted a hereditary patent of investiture.
translations.idiomatic: For his many achievements he was enfeoffed as a founding minister who supports the state through sincere martial service, with the titles Grand Master for Glorious Emolument and Pillar of the State, made Marquis of Xiping with a stipend of 2,500 shi, and granted a hereditary patent of investiture.

sentences.zh: 明年拜征西將軍，討西番，敗之土門峽。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed General on the Western Expedition to campaign against the western tribes and defeated them at Tumen Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made general on the western expedition, marched against the western tribes, and routed them at Tumen Gorge.

sentences.zh: 徑洮州，獲其長阿昌失納，築城東籠山，擊擒酋長三副使癭嗉子等，平朵甘納兒七站，拓地數千里，俘男女二萬、雜畜二十余萬，乃班師。

translations.literal: He pressed on to Taozhou, captured their leader Achangshina, built a fort on Donglong Mountain, struck and captured the chieftains' three vice-envoys Yingsuozi and others, pacified the seven stations of Duogannar, extended territory by several thousand li, took captive twenty thousand men and women and more than two hundred thousand assorted livestock, and then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to Taozhou, captured their leader Achangshina, built a fort on Donglong Mountain, defeated and captured the chieftains' three vice-envoys including Yingsuozi, pacified the seven stations of Duogannar, extended Ming territory by thousands of li, took twenty thousand men and women captive along with more than two hundred thousand head of livestock, and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 元國公脫火赤等屯和林，數擾邊。

translations.literal: Yuan princes such as Tuo Huozhe were encamped at Karakorum and repeatedly harassed the border.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan princes such as Tuo Huozhe were encamped at Karakorum and repeatedly raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 十三年命英總陝西兵出塞，略亦集乃路，渡黃河，登賀蘭山，涉流沙，七日至其境。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Ying was ordered to command Shaanxi troops beyond the frontier, overran the Yijinai route, crossed the Yellow River, ascended Helan Mountain, crossed drifting sands, and reached their territory in seven days.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Ying was ordered to lead Shaanxi troops beyond the frontier; he overran the Yijinai route, crossed the Yellow River, climbed Helan Mountain, crossed drifting sands, and reached enemy territory in seven days.

sentences.zh: 分四翼夜擊之，而自以驍騎沖其中堅。

translations.literal: He divided into four wings and attacked by night, while he himself with elite cavalry charged the enemy center.
translations.idiomatic: He split his force into four wings and struck by night, while he himself led elite cavalry straight at the enemy center.

sentences.zh: 擒脫火赤及知院愛足等，獲其全部以歸。

translations.literal: He captured Tuo Huozhe and Court Commissioner Aizhu among others and returned with their entire force.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Tuo Huozhe and Court Commissioner Aizhu among others and returned with their entire following.

sentences.zh: 明年，又從大將軍北征，異道出塞，略公主山長寨，克全寧四部，度臚朐河，執知院李宣，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: The next year he again followed the Grand General on the northern expedition, taking a separate route beyond the frontier, overran the long stockade at Gongzhu Mountain, subdued the four divisions of Quanning, crossed the Lüju River, seized Court Commissioner Li Xuan, and captured all his followers.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he again joined the grand general on the northern expedition, marching out by a separate route; he overran the long stockade at Gongzhu Mountain, subdued the four divisions of Quanning, crossed the Lüju River, seized Court Commissioner Li Xuan, and took all his followers captive.

sentences.zh: 尋拜征南右副將軍，同永昌侯藍玉從將軍傅友德取雲南。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Right Vice General on the Southern Expedition and, together with Marquis of Yongchang Lan Yu, followed General Fu Youde to take Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made right vice general on the southern expedition and, together with Marquis of Yongchang Lan Yu, followed General Fu Youde to conquer Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 元梁王遣平章達裏麻以兵十余萬拒于曲靖。

translations.literal: The Yuan Prince of Liang sent Pingzhang Dalima with more than a hundred thousand troops to resist at Qujing.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan Prince of Liang sent Pingzhang Dalima with more than a hundred thousand men to hold Qujing.

sentences.zh: 英乘霧趨白石江。

translations.literal: Ying took advantage of fog to hurry to the Baishi River.
translations.idiomatic: Ying used the cover of fog to rush to the Baishi River.

sentences.zh: 霧霽，兩軍相望，達裏麻大驚。

translations.literal: When the fog cleared the two armies faced each other; Dalima was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When the fog lifted the two armies stood face to face, and Dalima was badly shaken.

sentences.zh: 友德欲渡江，英曰：「我兵罷，懼為所扼。」

translations.literal: Youde wished to cross the river; Ying said: "Our troops are exhausted—we fear being choked off.
translations.idiomatic: Youde wanted to cross the river at once, but Ying said, "Our men are spent—we'll be strangled if we try.

sentences.zh: 乃帥諸軍嚴陳，若將渡者。

translations.literal: So he led the troops in a tight formation as if about to cross.
translations.idiomatic: So he drew up his troops in tight order, as though he meant to ford the river.

sentences.zh: 而奇兵從下流濟，出其陳後，張疑幟山谷間，人吹一銅角。

translations.literal: Meanwhile surprise troops crossed downstream and emerged behind their formation; deceptive banners were spread through the valleys, and each man blew a bronze horn.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile his surprise force crossed downstream and struck from behind; decoy banners filled the valleys, and every man blew a bronze horn.

sentences.zh: 元兵驚擾。

translations.literal: The Yuan troops were thrown into panic and confusion.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan army broke into panic and confusion.

sentences.zh: 英急麾軍渡江，以善泅者先之，長刀斫其軍。

translations.literal: Ying urgently waved his troops across the river, sending strong swimmers ahead, who slashed at the enemy with long knives.
translations.idiomatic: Ying immediately ordered the crossing, sending the best swimmers ahead to hack at the enemy with long knives.

sentences.zh: 軍卻，師畢濟。

translations.literal: The enemy army fell back, and the whole force finished crossing.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fell back, and the whole army got across.

sentences.zh: 鏖戰良久，復縱鐵騎，遂大敗之，生擒達裏麻，僵屍十餘里。

translations.literal: After fierce fighting lasting a long time, he again unleashed armored cavalry and utterly routed them, capturing Dalima alive; corpses lay stiff for more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: After a long, savage fight he unleashed his armored cavalry and broke them completely, taking Dalima alive; the dead lay stiff for more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 長驅入雲南，梁王走死，右丞觀音保以城降，屬郡皆下。

translations.literal: They drove deep into Yunnan; the Prince of Liang fled and died; Right Chancellor Guanyin Bao surrendered the city, and all subordinate prefectures fell.
translations.idiomatic: They swept deep into Yunnan; the Prince of Liang fled to his death; Right Chancellor Guanyin Bao surrendered the city, and every subordinate prefecture submitted.

sentences.zh: 獨大理倚點蒼山、洱海，扼龍首、龍尾二關。

translations.literal: Only Dali, relying on Cangshan and Erhai Lake, controlled the two passes of Longshou and Longwei.
translations.idiomatic: Only Dali remained, sheltered by Cangshan and Erhai Lake and holding the two passes of Longshou and Longwei.

sentences.zh: 關故南詔築，土酋段世守之。

translations.literal: The passes had been built in former times by Nanzhao; the native chieftain Duan Shi held them.
translations.idiomatic: The passes had been built long ago by Nanzhao, and the native chieftain Duan Shi now held them.

sentences.zh: 英自將抵下關，遣王弼由洱水東趨上關，胡海由石門間道渡河，扳點蒼山而上，立旗幟。

translations.literal: Ying personally led the force to Xianguan; he sent Wang Bi east along Erhai toward Shangguan, and Hu Hai by a secret route through Shimen to cross the river, climb Cangshan, and raise banners.
translations.idiomatic: Ying himself led the main force to Xianguan; he sent Wang Bi east along Erhai toward Shangguan, and Hu Hai by a hidden route through Shimen to cross the river, climb Cangshan, and raise banners.

sentences.zh: 英亂流斬關進，山上軍亦馳下，夾擊，擒段世，遂拔大理。

translations.literal: Ying crossed the current in disorder, cut through the pass and advanced; the troops on the mountain also galloped down, and in a pincer attack they captured Duan Shi and took Dali.
translations.idiomatic: Ying fought through the swirling current, broke the pass, and pressed forward while the troops on the mountain charged down; caught in the pincer, Duan Shi was captured and Dali fell.

sentences.zh: 分兵收未附諸蠻，設官立衛守之。

translations.literal: He divided troops to subdue unsubdued tribes, established officials and garrisons to hold them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent detachments to bring in tribes still holding out, then appointed officials and established garrisons to hold the region.

sentences.zh: 回軍，與友德會滇池，分道平烏撒、東川、建昌、芒部諸蠻，立烏撒、畢節二衛。

translations.literal: Returning, he joined Youde at Dianchi Lake, and by separate routes pacified the tribes of Wusa, Dongchuan, Jianchang, and Mangbu, establishing the two garrisons of Wusa and Bijie.
translations.idiomatic: On the march back he joined Youde at Dianchi Lake; by separate routes they pacified the tribes of Wusa, Dongchuan, Jianchang, and Mangbu and established the garrisons of Wusa and Bijie.

sentences.zh: 土酋楊苴等復煽諸蠻二十余萬圍雲南城。

translations.literal: Native chieftains such as Yang Ju again incited more than two hundred thousand tribesmen to besiege Yunnan City.
translations.idiomatic: Native chieftains such as Yang Ju again stirred up more than two hundred thousand tribesmen to besiege Yunnan City.

sentences.zh: 英馳救，蠻潰竄山谷中，分兵捕滅之，斬級六萬。

translations.literal: Ying raced to the rescue; the tribes scattered and fled into the valleys; he divided troops to hunt them down, taking sixty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Ying raced to the rescue; the tribes broke and fled into the mountains; he sent detachments to hunt them down and took sixty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 明年詔友德及玉班師，而留英鎮滇中。

translations.literal: The next year an edict ordered Youde and Yu to withdraw, while Ying was left to hold Dianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict recalled Youde and Yu, while Ying was left to hold Dianzhong.

sentences.zh: 十七年，曲靖亦佐酋作亂，討降之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the chieftain Yizuo at Qujing rebelled; Ying campaigned and subdued him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the chieftain Yizuo at Qujing rebelled; Ying marched against him and forced his submission.

sentences.zh: 因定普定、廣南諸蠻，通田州糧道。

translations.literal: Thereupon he settled the tribes of Puding and Guangnan and opened the grain route to Tianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then pacified the tribes of Puding and Guangnan and secured the grain route to Tianzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十年平浪穹蠻，奉詔自永寧至大理，六十里設一堡，留軍屯田。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he pacified the Pinglangqiong tribes; by imperial order he established a fort every sixty li from Yongning to Dali and left troops to farm garrison lands.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he pacified the Pinglangqiong tribes; by imperial order he built a fort every sixty li from Yongning to Dali and left troops to farm the garrison lands.

sentences.zh: 明年，百夷思倫發叛，誘群蠻入寇摩沙勒寨，遣都督甯正擊破之。

translations.literal: The next year the Baiyi chieftain Silunfa rebelled, inciting the tribes to raid Mosha Stockade; Ying sent Regional Commander Ning Zheng, who broke them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Baiyi chieftain Silunfa rebelled and incited the tribes to raid Mosha Stockade; Ying sent Regional Commander Ning Zheng, who defeated them.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，思倫發復寇定邊，眾號三十萬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Silunfa again raided Dingbian; his force was said to number three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Silunfa raided Dingbian again with a force said to number three hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 英選騎三萬馳救，置火砲勁弩為三行。

translations.literal: Ying selected thirty thousand cavalry and raced to the rescue, arranging cannon and powerful crossbows in three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Ying chose thirty thousand cavalry and raced to the rescue, deploying cannon and heavy crossbows in three ranks.

sentences.zh: 蠻驅百象，被甲荷欄楯，左右挾大竹為筒，筒置標槍，銳甚。

translations.literal: The tribes drove a hundred elephants, armored and bearing shields; on either side they carried great bamboo tubes, each tube holding a javelin, very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes drove a hundred elephants forward in armor with shields on their backs; men on either side carried great bamboo tubes fitted with javelins—formidable weapons.

sentences.zh: 英分軍為三，都督馮誠將前軍，甯正將左，都指揮同知湯昭將右。

translations.literal: Ying divided his army into three: Regional Commander Feng Cheng led the vanguard, Ning Zheng the left, and Vice Commander Tang Zhao the right.
translations.idiomatic: Ying split his army into three wings: Regional Commander Feng Cheng led the vanguard, Ning Zheng the left, and Vice Commander Tang Zhao the right.

sentences.zh: 將戰，令曰：「今日之事，有進無退。」

translations.literal: On the eve of battle he ordered: "In today's fight there is advance but no retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Before the battle he gave the order: "Today there is only forward—no falling back.

sentences.zh: 因乘風大呼，礮弩併發，象皆反走。

translations.literal: Then, riding the wind, he shouted loudly; artillery and crossbows fired together, and all the elephants turned and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Then, with the wind at their backs, his men shouted as artillery and crossbows opened fire together; the elephants all wheeled and fled.

sentences.zh: 昔剌亦者，寇梟將也，殊死鬥，左軍小卻。

translations.literal: Xilaye was a fierce enemy commander; fighting to the death, he forced the left wing to fall back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Xilaye, a fierce enemy commander, fought to the death and briefly drove the left wing back.

sentences.zh: 英登高望之，取佩刀，命左右斬帥首來。

translations.literal: Ying climbed high to watch, drew his belt dagger, and ordered his attendants to bring him the left commander's head.
translations.idiomatic: Ying climbed to a vantage point, drew the dagger at his belt, and ordered his attendants to bring him the left commander's head.

sentences.zh: 左帥見一人握刀馳下，恐，奮呼突陣。

translations.literal: The left commander saw a man gripping a blade gallop down toward him, was frightened, and with a fierce shout charged the enemy line.
translations.idiomatic: The left commander saw a man with a drawn blade galloping toward him, took fright, and with a fierce shout charged the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 大軍乘之，斬馘四萬餘人，生獲三十七象，餘象盡殪。

translations.literal: The main army pressed the advantage, beheading more than forty thousand men, capturing thirty-seven elephants alive, and killing all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The main army pressed the advantage, killing more than forty thousand men, capturing thirty-seven elephants alive, and slaughtering all the rest.

sentences.zh: 賊渠帥各被百餘矢，伏象背以死。

translations.literal: Each rebel chieftain had taken more than a hundred arrows and died slumped over an elephant's back.
translations.idiomatic: Each rebel chieftain had taken more than a hundred arrows and died sprawled across an elephant's back.

sentences.zh: 思倫發遁去，諸蠻震懼，麓川始不復梗。

translations.literal: Silunfa escaped; the tribes were shaken with fear, and Lucuan ceased to obstruct thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Silunfa fled; the tribes were terrified, and Lucuan never again blocked the frontier.

sentences.zh: 已，會穎國公傅友德討平東川蠻，又平越州酋阿資及廣西阿赤部。

translations.literal: Later he joined Duke of Yingguo Fu Youde in suppressing the Dongchuan tribes, and also pacified the Yuezhou chieftain Azi and the Achi clans of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Duke of Yingguo Fu Youde in putting down the Dongchuan tribes, and also pacified the Yuezhou chieftain Azi and the Achi clans of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，入朝，賜宴奉天殿，賚黃金二百兩、白金五千兩、鈔五百錠、彩幣百疋，遣還。

translations.literal: That winter he came to court, was granted a banquet in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, bestowed two hundred taels of gold, five thousand taels of silver, five hundred ingots of paper money, and a hundred bolts of colored silk, and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he came to court, was feasted in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, and was given two hundred taels of gold, five thousand taels of silver, five hundred ingots of paper money, and a hundred bolts of colored silk before being sent back.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，帝親拊之曰：「使我高枕無南顧憂者，汝英也。」

translations.literal: On taking leave at the palace steps, the emperor personally patted him and said: "The one who lets me sleep soundly without looking south in worry is you, Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When he took his leave at the palace steps, the emperor personally clasped his shoulder and said, "You, Ying, are the one who lets me sleep at ease without fear for the south.

sentences.zh: 還鎮，再敗百夷于景東。

translations.literal: Returning to his post, he again defeated the Baiyi at Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: Back at his post, he defeated the Baiyi again at Jingdong.

sentences.zh: 思倫發乞降，貢方物。

translations.literal: Silunfa begged to surrender and sent tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: Silunfa sued for peace and sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 阿資又叛，擊降之。

translations.literal: Azi rebelled again; Ying struck and subdued him.
translations.idiomatic: When Azi rebelled again, Ying marched against him and forced his submission.

sentences.zh: 南中悉定。

translations.literal: All of the south was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The whole south was finally pacified.

sentences.zh: 使使以兵威諭降諸番，番部有重譯入貢者。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to announce surrender under military might to the various frontier peoples; some tribal groups sent tribute through multiple layers of translation.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to bring the frontier peoples to heel by force of arms; some tribes even sent tribute through chains of interpreters.

sentences.zh: 二十五年六月，聞皇太子薨，哭極哀。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year, hearing that the crown prince had died, he wept with extreme grief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year, when he heard that the crown prince had died, he wept with overwhelming grief.

sentences.zh: 初，高皇后崩，英哭至嘔血。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Empress Gao died, Ying wept until he vomited blood.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Gao had died earlier, Ying had wept until he vomited blood.

sentences.zh: 至是感疾，卒於鎮，年四十八。

translations.literal: At this he fell ill from grief and died at his post, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Grief brought on illness, and he died at his post at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 軍民巷哭，遠夷皆為流涕。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians wept in the streets; distant tribes all shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians wept in the streets, and even distant tribes shed tears.

sentences.zh: 歸葬京師，追封黔甯王，諡昭靖，侑享太廟。

translations.literal: His body was returned for burial in the capital; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qianning, given the posthumous title Zhaojing, and granted a place in the imperial ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: His body was brought back to the capital for burial; he was posthumously made Prince of Qianning with the posthumous title Zhaojing and granted a place in the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 英沉毅寡言笑，好賢禮士，撫卒伍有恩，未嘗妄殺。

translations.literal: Ying was deep and resolute, sparing of speech and laughter, fond of the worthy and courteous to scholars, gracious in treating his troops, and never killed recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was grave and resolute, sparing of speech and laughter; he honored the worthy and treated scholars with courtesy, showed real kindness to his troops, and never killed without cause.

sentences.zh: 在滇，百務具舉，簡守令，課農桑，歲較屯田增損以為賞罰，墾田至百萬餘畝。

translations.literal: In Yunnan he attended to every branch of administration, selected magistrates, promoted farming and sericulture, each year compared gains and losses in garrison farming for rewards and punishments, and opened more than a million mu of land.
translations.idiomatic: In Yunnan he saw to every branch of government, chose magistrates carefully, promoted farming and sericulture, judged officials each year by the gains and losses of garrison farming, and opened more than a million mu of land.

sentences.zh: 滇池隘，浚而廣之，無復水患。

translations.literal: Dianchi Lake was constricted; he dredged and widened it, and flooding ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Dianchi Lake was choked and narrow; he dredged and widened it until the floods stopped.

sentences.zh: 通鹽井之利以來商旅，辨方物以定貢稅，視民數以均力役。
