translations.literal: He opened the profits of salt wells to draw merchants and travelers, distinguished local products to fix tribute and taxes, and measured the population to equalize labor service.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the salt wells to trade and drew merchants in; he catalogued local products to fix tribute and taxes, and apportioned labor service according to population.

sentences.zh: 疏節闊目，民以便安。

translations.literal: His regulations were broad and his measures sparing; the people found ease and security.
translations.idiomatic: His rules were simple and his demands light, and the people lived in ease and security.

sentences.zh: 居常讀書不釋卷，暇則延諸儒生講說經史。

translations.literal: In daily life he read without setting his books down; in leisure he invited Confucian scholars to lecture on the classics and history.
translations.idiomatic: He read constantly and never put his books aside; in his free time he invited Confucian scholars to lecture on the classics and history.

sentences.zh: 太祖初起時，數養他姓為子，攻下郡邑，輒遣之出守，多至二十餘人，惟英在西南勳最大。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor first rose, he repeatedly adopted sons of other surnames; whenever a prefecture or county was taken he would send them out to govern, until there were more than twenty; only Ying's achievements in the southwest were greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor first rose to power he repeatedly adopted sons of other surnames and, as counties and prefectures fell, sent them out to govern until there were more than twenty such men; of them all, only Ying's achievements in the southwest were greatest.

sentences.zh: 子春、晟、昂皆鎮雲南。

translations.literal: His sons Chun, Sheng, and Ang all held Yunnan in command.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Chun, Sheng, and Ang all held command in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 昕駙馬都尉，尚成祖女常甯公主。

translations.literal: Xin was Commandant-in-Chief of the Horse and married Emperor Chengzu's daughter, Princess Changning.
translations.idiomatic: Xin served as Commandant-in-Chief of the Horse and married Emperor Chengzu's daughter, Princess Changning.

sentences.zh: 春，字景春，材武有父風。

translations.literal: Chun, courtesy name Jingchun, was talented in martial affairs and had his father's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, whose courtesy name was Jingchun, was gifted in arms and bore his father's stamp.

sentences.zh: 年十七，從英征西番，又從征雲南，從平江西寇，皆先登。

translations.literal: At seventeen he followed Ying on the western campaign, then on the Yunnan campaign, and on the suppression of Jiangxi bandits, always first over the wall.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he followed Ying against the western tribes, then on the Yunnan campaign, and on the suppression of Jiangxi bandits—always first over the wall.

sentences.zh: 積功授後軍都督府僉事。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he was appointed Commissioner of the Rear Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated merit he was made Commissioner of the Rear Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 群臣請試職，帝曰：「兒，我家人，勿試也。」

translations.literal: The ministers asked that he be tried in office; the emperor said: "The boy is family to me—do not put him on trial.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers asked that he serve a probationary term, the emperor said, "The boy is one of my own—no trial appointment for him.

sentences.zh: 遂予實授。

translations.literal: So he was given a full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the post outright.

sentences.zh: 嘗命錄烈山囚，又命鞫叛黨於蔚州，所開釋各數百人。

translations.literal: He was once ordered to review prisoners at Lieshan, and again to try rebels at Weizhou; in each case he released several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He was once ordered to review prisoners at Lieshan and again to try rebels at Weizhou; each time he released several hundred people.

sentences.zh: 英卒，命嗣爵，鎮雲南。

translations.literal: When Ying died, Chun was ordered to inherit the title and hold Yunnan in command.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying died, he was ordered to inherit the title and take command in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六年，維摩十一寨亂，遣瞿能討平之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Hongwu the eleven stockades of Weimo rebelled; he sent Qu Neng to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Hongwu the eleven stockades of Weimo rebelled; he sent Qu Neng to put them down.

sentences.zh: 明年平越巂蠻，立瀾滄衛。

translations.literal: The next year he pacified the Yuexi tribes and established Lancang Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he pacified the Yuexi tribes and established the Lancang Garrison.

sentences.zh: 其冬，阿資復叛，與何福討之。

translations.literal: That winter Azi rebelled again; Chun joined He Fu in campaigning against him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when Azi rebelled again, he joined He Fu in campaigning against him.

sentences.zh: 春曰：「此賊積年逋誅者，以與諸土酋姻婭，輾轉亡匿。

translations.literal: Chun said: "This bandit has evaded execution for years because he is related by marriage to the native chieftains and has moved from hiding place to hiding place.
translations.idiomatic: Chun said, "This rebel has escaped punishment for years because he is tied by marriage to the native chieftains and keeps slipping from one hiding place to another.

sentences.zh: 今悉發諸酋從軍，縻系之，而多設營堡，制其出人，授首必矣。」

translations.literal: Now if we mobilize all the chieftains with the army, keep them under restraint, and set up many camps and forts to control their comings and goings, his head is sure to be delivered.
translations.idiomatic: If we now mobilize all the chieftains with the army, keep them under restraint, and build camps and forts everywhere to control their movements, his head is as good as delivered.

sentences.zh: 遂趨越州，分道逼其城，伏精兵道左，以羸卒誘賊，縱擊大敗之。

translations.literal: So he hurried to Yuezhou, pressed the city by separate routes, hid elite troops on the left of the road, used weak soldiers to lure the rebels, then unleashed an attack and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He then hurried to Yuezhou, closed on the city by separate routes, hid elite troops on the left of the road, baited the rebels with a weak detachment, and then struck and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 阿資亡穀中，春陰結旁近土官，詗知所在，樹壘斷其糧道。

translations.literal: Azi fled into a valley; Chun secretly contacted nearby native officials, learned where he was, and built stockades to cut off his grain route.
translations.idiomatic: Azi fled into a valley; Chun secretly contacted nearby native officials, learned where he was hiding, and built stockades to cut off his supply lines.

sentences.zh: 賊困甚。

translations.literal: The rebels were in extreme distress.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were driven to desperation.

sentences.zh: 已，出不意搗其巢，遂擒阿資，並誅其黨二百四十人。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, catching them off guard, he struck their nest, captured Azi, and executed two hundred forty of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Then, catching them off guard, he stormed their stronghold, captured Azi, and executed two hundred forty of his followers.

sentences.zh: 越州遂平。

translations.literal: Yuezhou was thereupon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 廣南酋儂貞佑糾黨蠻拒官軍，破擒之，俘斬千計。

translations.literal: The Guangnan chieftain Nong Zhenyou rallied tribal followers to resist the government army; Chun defeated and captured him, with captive killings numbering in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangnan chieftain Nong Zhenyou rallied tribal allies to resist the government troops; Chun defeated and captured him, taking and slaying thousands.

sentences.zh: 寧遠酋刀拜爛依交址不順命，遣何福討降之。

translations.literal: The Ningyuan chieftain Dao Bailan, relying on Jiaozhi, refused to obey orders; Chun sent He Fu to campaign against and subdue him.
translations.idiomatic: The Ningyuan chieftain Dao Bailan, leaning on Dai Viet for support, refused to obey orders; Chun sent He Fu to campaign against him and bring him to submission.

sentences.zh: 三十年，麓川宣慰使思倫發為其屬刀幹孟所逐。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, the Luchuan Pacification Commissioner Si Lunfa was driven out by his subordinate Dao Ganmeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Hongwu, the Luchuan Pacification Commissioner Si Lunfa was driven out by his subordinate Dao Ganmeng.

sentences.zh: 來奔。

translations.literal: He came in flight to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to the court for refuge.

sentences.zh: 春挾與俱朝，受上方略，遂拜春為征虜前將軍，帥何福、徐凱討之。

translations.literal: Chun brought him along to court, received the emperor's strategic plan, and was then appointed General-in-Chief for Subduing Barbarians of the Forward Army, leading He Fu and Xu Kai to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Chun brought him to court in his retinue, received the emperor's campaign plan, and was then appointed Forward General for Subduing Barbarians, commanding He Fu and Xu Kai against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 先以兵送思倫發于金齒，檄幹孟來迎。

translations.literal: First he sent troops to escort Si Lunfa to Jingchi and issued a summons for Ganmeng to come and receive him.
translations.idiomatic: First he sent troops to escort Si Lunfa to Jingchi and summoned Ganmeng to come and receive him.

sentences.zh: 不應。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Ganmeng did not respond.

sentences.zh: 乃選卒五千，令福與瞿能將，逾高良公山，直搗南甸，大破之，斬其酋刀名孟。

translations.literal: Thereupon he selected five thousand soldiers, had Fu and Qu Neng lead them over Mount Gaolianggong, struck straight at Nandian, routed them utterly, and beheaded their chieftain Dao Mingmeng.
translations.idiomatic: He then selected five thousand men and put Fu and Qu Neng in command; they crossed Mount Gaolianggong, struck straight at Nandian, routed the enemy, and beheaded the chieftain Dao Mingmeng.

sentences.zh: 回軍擊景罕寨。

translations.literal: On the return march the army attacked the stockade at Jinghan.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march they attacked the stockade at Jinghan.

sentences.zh: 賊乘高堅守，官軍糧且盡，福告急。

translations.literal: The rebels held the heights and defended tenaciously; the government army's provisions were nearly exhausted, and Fu sent an urgent appeal.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the high ground and defended stubbornly; government provisions were nearly exhausted, and Fu sent an urgent appeal for help.

sentences.zh: 春帥五百騎救之。

translations.literal: Chun led five hundred horsemen to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Chun led five hundred cavalry to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 夜渡怒江，旦抵寨，下令騎騁，揚塵蔽天，賊大驚潰。

translations.literal: He crossed the Nu River by night; at dawn he reached the stockade, ordered the horsemen to charge freely, raising dust that blotted out the sky; the rebels were greatly alarmed and fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Nu River by night and reached the stockade at dawn, then ordered his cavalry to charge at full gallop until the dust blotted out the sky; the rebels panicked and fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 乘勝擊崆峒寨，亦潰。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory, he attacked the Kongtong stockade, and it too collapsed in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing their advantage, they attacked the Kongtong stockade and broke that position as well.

sentences.zh: 前後降者七萬人。

translations.literal: Those who surrendered before and after numbered seventy thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: In all, seventy thousand people submitted.

sentences.zh: 將士欲屠之，春不可。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers wished to massacre them, but Chun would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers wanted to massacre them, but Chun forbade it.

sentences.zh: 幹孟乞降，帝不許，命春總滇、黔、蜀兵攻之。

translations.literal: Ganmeng begged to surrender; the emperor would not permit it and ordered Chun to muster the troops of Yunnan, Guizhou, and Sichuan to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Ganmeng begged to surrender, but the emperor refused and ordered Chun to assemble troops from Yunnan, Guizhou, and Sichuan for the attack.

sentences.zh: 末發而春卒，年三十六。

translations.literal: Before the campaign could be launched Chun died, at the age of thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Before the campaign could be launched, Chun died at the age of thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 諡惠襄。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Huixiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Huixiang.

sentences.zh: 春在鎮七年，大修屯政，辟田三十余萬畝，鑿鐵池河，灌宜良涸田數萬畝，民復業者五千餘戶，為立祠祀之。

translations.literal: During Chun's seven years in command he greatly expanded agricultural colonies, opening more than three hundred thousand mu of land, digging the Tiechi River to irrigate tens of thousands of mu of parched fields in Yiliang; more than five thousand households resumed livelihood, and a shrine was built to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: During his seven years in command, Chun greatly expanded military colonies, reclaiming more than three hundred thousand mu of land; he dug the Tiechi River to irrigate tens of thousands of mu of dried-out fields at Yiliang, helped more than five thousand households return to their livelihoods, and the people built a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟晟嗣。

translations.literal: He had no son; his younger brother Sheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son; his younger brother Sheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年，八百大甸寇邊，遏貢使，晟會車裏、木邦討定之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle the Eight Hundred Great Domains raided the frontier, blocking tribute envoys; Sheng joined with Cheli and Mubang to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongle, the Eight Hundred Great Domains raided the frontier and blocked tribute envoys; Sheng joined forces with Cheli and Mubang to put them down.

sentences.zh: 明年大發兵討交址，拜晟征夷左副將軍，與大將軍張輔異道自雲南入。

translations.literal: The next year a great force was mobilized to campaign against Jiaozhi; Sheng was appointed Left Vice General-in-Chief for Subduing Barbarians and, by a separate route from the Grand General Zhang Fu, entered from Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the court mobilized a great army against Dai Viet; Sheng was appointed Left Vice General for Subduing Barbarians and, taking a separate route from Grand General Zhang Fu, entered from Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 遂由蒙自徑野蒲斬木通道，奪猛烈、掤華諸關隘。

translations.literal: He then went from Mengzi straight through Yebu, cutting trees to open a passage, and seized the passes at Menglie, Binhua, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced from Mengzi straight through Yebu, cutting timber to clear a path, and seized the passes at Menglie, Binhua, and others.

sentences.zh: 舁舟夜出洮水，渡富良江，與輔會師。

translations.literal: He carried boats out onto the Tao River by night, crossed the Fu River, and joined forces with Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He carried boats out onto the Tao River by night, crossed the Fu River, and joined Zhang Fu.

sentences.zh: 共破多邦城，搗其東西二都，蕩諸巢，擒偽王黎季犛，語在《輔傳》。

translations.literal: Together they captured Duobang city, struck their eastern and western capitals, swept away the nest strongholds, and captured the false king Le Quy Ly; the account is in the Biography of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Together they took Duobang city, struck at the eastern and western capitals, swept away rebel strongholds, and captured the usurper Le Quy Ly; the fuller account appears in Zhang Fu's biography.

sentences.zh: 論功封黔國公，歲祿三千石，予世券。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qian, with three thousand shi of annual stipend and an hereditary patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qian, granted an annual stipend of three thousand shi, and given an hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 交址簡定復叛，命晟佩征夷將軍印討之，戰生厥江，敗績。

translations.literal: When Jian Ding of Jiaozhi rebelled again, Sheng was ordered to campaign against him bearing the seal of General for Subduing Barbarians; they fought at the Shengque River and suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian Ding rebelled again in Dai Viet, Sheng was ordered to campaign against him with the seal of General for Subduing Barbarians; they fought at the Shengque River and were defeated.

sentences.zh: 輔再出帥師合討，擒定送京師。

translations.literal: Fu again took command and joined forces for a joint campaign, captured Ding, and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu took command again and joined in a combined campaign, captured Jian Ding, and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 輔還，晟留捕陳季擴，連戰不能下。

translations.literal: Fu returned; Sheng remained to capture Chen Jikuo, but battle after battle failed to bring him down.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Fu returned, Sheng stayed behind to capture Chen Jikuo, but repeated battles failed to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 輔復出帥師會晟，窮追至占城，獲季擴，乃班師，晟亦受上賞。

translations.literal: Fu again took command and joined Sheng, pursued to the end at Champa, captured Jikuo, and then withdrew the army; Sheng also received high reward.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu took command again and joined Sheng, pursued the enemy all the way to Champa, captured Chen Jikuo, and then withdrew; Sheng also received generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 十七年，富州蠻叛，晟引兵臨之，弗攻，使人譬曉，竟下之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the tribes of Fuzhou rebelled; Sheng led troops to their borders but did not attack, sending men to explain and persuade, and they eventually submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the tribes of Fuzhou rebelled; Sheng marched his troops to their border but held his fire, sent envoys to reason with them, and in the end they submitted.

sentences.zh: 晟席父兄業，用兵非所長，戰數不利。

translations.literal: Sheng inherited the enterprise of his father and elder brother; military command was not his strength, and in battle he often met with ill fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had inherited the legacy of his father and elder brother, but military command was not his strength, and he often fared poorly in battle.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其絕遠，且世將，寬假之。

translations.literal: The court, because the region was extremely remote and because he was a hereditary commander, showed him leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Because the region was far away and he was a hereditary commander, the court treated him leniently.

sentences.zh: 而滇人懾晟父子威信，莊事如朝廷。

translations.literal: Yet the people of Yunnan stood in awe of the prestige of Sheng and his father, and conducted affairs with the same solemnity as at court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people of Yunnan stood in awe of the prestige of the Sheng father and son, and conducted affairs with the same formality as at court.

sentences.zh: 片楮下，土酋具威儀出郭迎，盥而後啟，曰：「此令旨也。」

translations.literal: When a single sheet of paper descended, the native chieftains assembled in full ceremonial dress to welcome it outside the city gate, washed their hands before opening it, and said: "This is an imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: When even a single sheet of paper arrived from him, native chieftains would turn out in full ceremonial dress to receive it outside the city gate, wash their hands before opening it, and say, "This is an imperial command.

sentences.zh: 晟久鎮，置田園三百六十區，資財充牣，善事朝貴，賂遺不絕，以故得中外聲。

translations.literal: Sheng held command for a long time, established three hundred sixty estates, possessed overflowing wealth, treated court nobles well, and sent bribes without cease; for this reason he enjoyed reputation both within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng held long command, amassed three hundred sixty estates, and possessed overflowing wealth; he cultivated court nobles with gifts that never ceased, and for this reason enjoyed reputation at court and in the provinces alike.

sentences.zh: 晟有子斌，字文輝，幼嗣公爵，居京師，而以昂代鎮。

translations.literal: Sheng had a son Bin, courtesy name Wenhui, who at a young age inherited the ducal title and resided in the capital, while Ang was put in his place to hold command.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had a son Bin, courtesy name Wenhui, who inherited the ducal title while still young and remained in the capital, while Ang was placed in command in his stead.

sentences.zh: 昂，字景高，初為府軍左衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Ang, courtesy name Jinggao, at first served as Assistant Commandant of the Left Guard of the Fufu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Ang, courtesy name Jinggao, initially served as assistant commandant of the Left Guard of the Fufu Army.

sentences.zh: 成祖將使晟南討，乃擢昂都指揮同知，領雲南都司，累遷至右都督。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor was about to send Sheng on a southern campaign, Ang was promoted to Vice Commandant-in-Chief and put in charge of the Yunnan Regional Military Commission, rising in succession to Right Chief Controller.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor was about to send Sheng on a southern campaign, Ang was promoted to vice commandant-in-chief and put in charge of the Yunnan Regional Military Commission, eventually rising to Right Chief Controller.

sentences.zh: 正統四年佩將印，討麓川，抵金齒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengtong he was granted the general's seal and campaigned against Luchuan, reaching Jingchi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhengtong he received the general's seal and campaigned against Luchuan, reaching Jingchi.

sentences.zh: 畏賊盛，遷延者久之。

translations.literal: Fearing the rebels' strength, he delayed for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the rebels' strength, he delayed for a long time.

sentences.zh: 參將張榮前驅至芒部敗，昂不救，引還，貶秩二級。

translations.literal: Vice General Zhang Rong, advancing as vanguard, was defeated at Mangbu; Ang did not rescue him but withdrew, and was demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Vice General Zhang Rong, advancing as vanguard, was defeated at Mangbu; Ang failed to relieve him and withdrew instead, and was demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 已，思任發入寇，擊卻之，又捕斬師宗反者。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Si Renfa invaded; Ang drove him back and also captured and executed rebels in Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when Si Renfa invaded, Ang drove him back and also captured and executed rebels in Shizong.

sentences.zh: 六年，兵部尚書王驥、定西伯蔣貴將大軍討思任發，昂主饋運。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Minister of War Wang Ji and the Earl of Dingxi Jiang Gui led a great army against Si Renfa; Ang was in charge of supply transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Minister of War Wang Ji and the Earl of Dingxi Jiang Gui led a great army against Si Renfa, with Ang in charge of supply transport.

sentences.zh: 賊破，復昂職，命督軍捕思任發，不能得。

translations.literal: When the rebels were defeated Ang's rank was restored; he was ordered to direct troops in the capture of Si Renfa but could not obtain him.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were defeated, Ang's rank was restored and he was ordered to hunt down Si Renfa, but failed to capture him.

sentences.zh: 十年，昂卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Ang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Ang died.

sentences.zh: 贈定邊伯，諡武襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Earl of Dingbian and given the posthumous title Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously created Earl of Dingbian and honored as Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 斌始之鎮，會緬甸執思任發送京師，其子思機發來襲，斌擊卻之。

translations.literal: When Bin first took command, Burma had just captured Si Renfa and sent him to the capital; his son Si Jifa came to attack, and Bin drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin first took command, Burma had just captured Si Renfa and sent him to the capital; his son Si Jifa then launched an attack, and Bin drove him back.

sentences.zh: 思機發復據孟養。

translations.literal: Si Jifa again occupied Mengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Si Jifa again seized Mengyang.

sentences.zh: 十三年復大發兵，使驥等討之，而斌為後拒，督餉無乏。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year a great army was again mobilized; Ji and others were sent to campaign against him, while Bin served as rear guard and supervised supplies without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the court mobilized a great army again; Wang Ji and others were sent against him, while Bin served as rear guard and kept the supplies flowing without fail.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太傅，諡榮康。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Grand Mentor and given the posthumous title Rongkang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Grand Mentor and honored as Rongkang.

sentences.zh: 子琮幼，景泰初，命昂孫璘以都督同知代鎮。

translations.literal: His son Cong was young; at the beginning of the Jingtai reign Lin, Ang's grandson, was ordered to hold command in his place as Vice Chief Controller.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cong was still young; at the beginning of the Jingtai reign Ang's grandson Lin was appointed vice chief controller to hold command in his stead.

sentences.zh: 璘字廷章，素儒雅，滇人易之，既而號令肅然不可犯，天順初卒。

translations.literal: Lin, courtesy name Tingzhang, had always been refined and scholarly; the people of Yunnan took him lightly, but once in command his orders were stern and not to be violated; he died at the beginning of the Tianshun reign.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, courtesy name Tingzhang, had always been refined and scholarly, and the people of Yunnan underestimated him at first; but once he took command his orders were stern and inviolable, and he died early in the Tianshun reign.

sentences.zh: 琮猶幼，擢璘弟錦衣副千戶瓚為都督同知，往代。

translations.literal: Cong was still young; Zan, Lin's younger brother and a Deputy Centurion of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, was promoted to Vice Chief Controller and sent to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was still young, so Zan, Lin's younger brother and a deputy centurion of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, was promoted to vice chief controller and sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 居七年，先後討平沾祿諸寨及土官之構兵者，降思卜發，勒還諸蠻侵地。

translations.literal: After seven years in command he successively suppressed the stockades of Zhanlu and native officials who had raised arms, reduced Sibufa to submission, and compelled the return of lands seized by various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Over seven years in command he successively suppressed the stockades of Zhanlu and native officials who had taken up arms, brought Sibufa to submission, and compelled the return of lands seized by various tribes.

sentences.zh: 功多，然頗黷貨。

translations.literal: His achievements were many, yet he was rather greedy for goods.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were many, yet he was rather corrupt.

sentences.zh: 成化三年春，琮始之鎮，而以瓚為副總兵，移鎮金齒。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Chenghua Cong first took command, while Zan was made Vice Commander-in-Chief and transferred to hold Jingchi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Chenghua, Cong took command for the first time, while Zan was made vice commander-in-chief and transferred to Jingchi.

sentences.zh: 琮字廷芳，通經義，能詞章，屬夷饋贄無所受。

translations.literal: Cong, courtesy name Tingfang, was versed in the classics and capable in literary composition; when tribes submitted gifts he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, courtesy name Tingfang, was versed in the classics and skilled in literary composition, and refused all gifts offered by submitting tribes.

sentences.zh: 尋甸酋殺兄子，求為守，琮捕誅之。

translations.literal: The Xundian chieftain killed his elder brother's son and sought to be appointed local commander; Cong captured and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xundian chieftain killed his elder brother's son and sought appointment as local commander; Cong captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 廣西土官虐，所部為亂，琮請更設流官，民大便。

translations.literal: The native official of Guangxi was cruel and his jurisdiction fell into disorder; Cong requested that regular officials be reappointed, greatly to the people's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The native official of Guangxi was cruel and his jurisdiction fell into disorder; Cong petitioned to replace him with regular officials, greatly to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 以次討平馬龍、麗江、劍川、順甯、羅雄諸叛蠻，捕擒橋甸、南窩反者。

translations.literal: In succession he suppressed rebellious tribes at Malong, Lijiang, Jianchuan, Shunning, and Luoxiong, and captured rebels at Qiaodian and Nanwo.
translations.idiomatic: In succession he put down rebellious tribes at Malong, Lijiang, Jianchuan, Shunning, and Luoxiong, and captured rebels at Qiaodian and Nanwo.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太師，諡武僖。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and honored as Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 無子，以瓚孫昆嗣。

translations.literal: He had no son; Kun, Zan's grandson, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son; Zan's grandson Kun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 昆字元中，初襲錦衣指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Kun, courtesy name Yuanzhong, at first inherited the post of Assistant Commandant of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Kun, courtesy name Yuanzhong, initially inherited the post of assistant commandant of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 琮撫為子，朝議以昆西平侯裔孫當嗣侯，而守臣爭之，謂滇人知黔國公不知西平侯也，侯之恐為所輕。

translations.literal: Cong had raised him as a son; court deliberation held that as a descendant of the Marquis of Xiping, Kun ought to inherit the marquisate, but the frontier officials disputed this, saying the people of Yunnan knew the Duke of Qian but not the Marquis of Xiping, and feared the marquisate would be slighted.
translations.idiomatic: Cong had raised him as a son; court deliberation held that as a descendant of the Marquis of Xiping, Kun ought to inherit the marquisate, but local officials objected, arguing that the people of Yunnan knew the Duke of Qian but not the Marquis of Xiping, and that the lesser title might be disrespected.

sentences.zh: 孝宗以為然，令嗣公，佩印如故。

translations.literal: The Xiaozong Emperor agreed and ordered him to succeed to the ducal title, bearing the seal as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong agreed and ordered him to succeed as duke, bearing the seal as before.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年平龜山、竹箐諸蠻，又平普安賊，再益歲祿。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi he pacified the tribes of Guishan and Zhujing, then pacified rebels at Pu'an, and his annual stipend was increased again.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi he pacified the tribes of Guishan and Zhujing, then put down rebels at Pu'an, and his annual stipend was increased again.

sentences.zh: 正德二年，師宗民阿本作亂，與都御史吳文度督兵分三道進。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde the commoner Aben of Shizong rebelled; Kun joined Censor-in-Chief Wu Wendu in directing troops advancing by three routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde, when the commoner Aben of Shizong rebelled, Kun joined Censor-in-Chief Wu Wendu in directing a three-pronged advance.

sentences.zh: 一出師宗，一出羅雄，一出彌勒，而別遣一軍伏盤江，截賊巢，遂大破之。

translations.literal: One force came out from Shizong, one from Luoxiong, one from Mile, while another army was separately deployed in ambush at the Pan River to cut off the rebel nest, and they utterly routed them.
translations.idiomatic: One column advanced from Shizong, one from Luoxiong, one from Mile, while a separate force lay in ambush at the Pan River to cut off the rebel stronghold, and together they routed the enemy completely.

sentences.zh: 七年，安南長官司那代爭襲，殺土官，復與都御史顧源討擒之，再加太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Annam Chief Office's Nadai disputed succession, killed the native official, and Kun again joined Censor-in-Chief Gu Yuan in campaigning and capturing him, and was further made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when Nadai of the Annam Chief Office disputed succession and killed the native official, Kun again joined Censor-in-Chief Gu Yuan to campaign against him and capture him, and was further promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 昆初喜文學，自矜厲，其後通賂權近，所請無不得。

translations.literal: At first Kun delighted in literary studies and was strict with himself; afterward he bribed those close to power, and whatever he requested he obtained.
translations.idiomatic: At first Kun delighted in literary studies and held himself to a strict standard; later he bribed those close to power, and whatever he asked for he obtained.

sentences.zh: 浸驕，淩三司，使從角門入。

translations.literal: Gradually he grew arrogant, looked down on the three commissions, and made them enter by the side gate.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually he grew arrogant, looked down on the three provincial commissions, and made them enter by the side gate.

sentences.zh: 諸言官論劾者，輒得罪去。

translations.literal: Whenever censorial officials impeached him, they promptly met with punishment and departure.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever censorial officials impeached him, they were promptly punished and driven from office.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太師，諡莊襄。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Zhuangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and honored as Zhuangxiang.

sentences.zh: 子紹勳嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shaoxun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shaoxun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 尋甸土舍安銓叛，都御史傅習討之，敗績。

translations.literal: An Quan, a native officer of Xundian, rebelled; Censor-in-Chief Fu Xi campaigned against him and suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: An Quan, a native officer of Xundian, rebelled; Censor-in-Chief Fu Xi campaigned against him and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 武定土舍鳳朝文亦叛，與銓連兵攻雲南，大擾。

translations.literal: Feng Chaowen, a native officer of Wuding, also rebelled; joining forces with Quan he attacked Yunnan and caused great disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Chaowen, a native officer of Wuding, also rebelled; joining forces with Quan he attacked Yunnan and threw the province into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 世宗遣尚書伍文定將大軍征之。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor sent Minister Wu Wendeng at the head of a great army to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong sent Minister Wu Wendeng at the head of a great army to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 未至，而紹勳督所部先進，告土官子弟當襲者，先予冠帶，破賊後當為請。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Shaoxun directed his own troops in advance, telling native officials' sons due to inherit that if they were given caps and belts first, he would petition on their behalf after the rebels were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wu Wendeng arrived, Shaoxun led his own troops forward in advance, promising the sons of native officials due to inherit that if they received official caps and belts now, he would petition on their behalf once the rebels were defeated.

sentences.zh: 眾多奮戰，賊大敗。

translations.literal: Many fought with renewed zeal; the rebels were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Many fought with renewed zeal, and the rebels were routed.

sentences.zh: 朝文絕普渡河走，追斬之東川。

translations.literal: Chaowen fled across the Pu River; he was pursued and beheaded at Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chaowen fled across the Pu River; he was pursued and beheaded at Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 銓還尋甸，列砦數十，官軍攻破之，擒銓於芒部。

translations.literal: Quan returned to Xundian and set up several dozen stockades; the government army broke through them and captured Quan at Mangbu.
translations.idiomatic: Quan retreated to Xundian and set up dozens of stockades; government troops broke through them and captured Quan at Mangbu.

sentences.zh: 先後擒賊党千餘人，俘斬無算。

translations.literal: Before and after they captured more than a thousand rebel followers; captive killings were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In all they captured more than a thousand rebel followers, with captures and killings beyond count.

sentences.zh: 時嘉靖七年也。

translations.literal: This was in the seventh year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the seventh year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，加太子太傅，益歲祿。

translations.literal: When victory was reported he was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and his annual stipend was increased.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, he was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and his annual stipend was increased.

sentences.zh: 而是時老撾、木邦、孟養、緬甸、孟密相仇殺，師宗、納樓、思陀、八寨皆亂，久不解。

translations.literal: Yet at this time Laos, Mubang, Mengyang, Burma, and Mengmi were mutually killing one another; Shizong, Nalou, Situo, and Bazhai were all in disorder, long unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at this time Laos, Mubang, Mengyang, Burma, and Mengmi were locked in mutual bloodshed; Shizong, Nalou, Situo, and Bazhai were all in revolt, and the unrest dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 紹勳使使者遍曆諸蠻，諷以武定、尋甸事，皆懾伏，願還侵地，而木邦、孟養俱貢方物謝罪。

translations.literal: Shaoxun sent envoys to tour all the tribes, hinting at the affairs of Wuding and Xundian; all were awed into submission, wished to return seized lands, and Mubang and Mengyang both sent local products in tribute to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxun sent envoys throughout the tribes, pointing to what had happened at Wuding and Xundian; all were awed into submission, offered to return seized lands, and Mubang and Mengyang both sent tribute goods to apologize.

sentences.zh: 南中悉定。

translations.literal: All of the south was thereupon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The entire south was pacified.

sentences.zh: 紹勳有勇略，用兵輒勝。

translations.literal: Shaoxun had courage and strategy; whenever he employed troops he prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxun had courage and strategic skill; whenever he took the field he prevailed.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太師，諡敏靖。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Minjing.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and honored as Minjing.

sentences.zh: 子朝輔嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chaofu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chaofu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 都御史劉渠索賂，朝輔與之，因上章言：「臣家世守茲土，上下相承。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Liu Qu demanded a bribe; Chaofu gave it to him and then submitted a memorial saying: "My family has guarded this land for generations, one generation succeeding another.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Liu Qu demanded a bribe, and Chaofu paid it; he then submitted a memorial saying, "My family has guarded this land for generations, each generation succeeding the last.

sentences.zh: 今有司紛更典制，關臣職守，率不與聞，接見不循故例。

translations.literal: Now the local officials have repeatedly changed regulations touching my duties, generally without informing me, and audiences no longer follow former precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Now local officials keep changing regulations that bear on my duties, usually without informing me, and audiences no longer follow the old precedents.

sentences.zh: 臣疏遠孤危，動作掣肘，無以彈壓蠻方。

translations.literal: I am distant, isolated, and imperiled; in every action I am checked and hindered, and cannot suppress the tribal regions.
translations.idiomatic: I am far from court, isolated, and vulnerable; at every turn I am checked and hindered, and cannot keep the tribal frontier under control.

sentences.zh: 乞申敕諸臣，悉如其舊。」

translations.literal: I beg that all officials be expressly commanded to restore everything as before.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that all officials be expressly ordered to restore everything as it was before.

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his request.

sentences.zh: 給事中萬虞愷劾朝輔，並論渠。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wan Yukai impeached Chaofu and also censured Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wan Yukai impeached Chaofu and also censured Liu Qu.

sentences.zh: 詔罷渠而令朝輔治事如故。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed Qu and ordered Chaofu to administer affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dismissed Liu Qu and ordered Chaofu to continue in office as before.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太保，諡恭僖。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Grand Guardian and given the posthumous title Gongxi.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Grand Guardian and honored as Gongxi.

sentences.zh: 二子融、鞏皆幼。

translations.literal: His two sons Rong and Gong were both young.
translations.idiomatic: Both his sons, Rong and Gong, were still young.

sentences.zh: 詔視琮、璘故事，令融嗣公，給半祿，而授朝輔弟朝弼都督僉事，佩印代鎮。

translations.literal: An edict looked to the precedents of Cong and Lin, ordered Rong to succeed to the dukedom and granted half stipend, while appointing Chaofu's younger brother Chaob as Assistant Chief Controller with seal to hold command in his place.
translations.idiomatic: An edict, following the precedents set for Cong and Lin, ordered Rong to succeed to the ducal title with half stipend, while Chaofu's younger brother Chaob was appointed assistant chief controller, given the seal, and sent to hold command in his stead.

sentences.zh: 居三年，融卒，鞏當嗣，朝弼心害之，於是朝弼嫡母李請護鞏居京師，待其長而還鎮。

translations.literal: After three years Rong died; Gong was to succeed, and Chaob resented this in his heart; thereupon Chaob's principal mother Lady Li petitioned to have Gong protected and kept in the capital, to return to hold command once he came of age.
translations.idiomatic: After three years Rong died and Gong was due to succeed; Chaob resented this, whereupon his principal mother, Lady Li, petitioned to have Gong kept under guard in the capital until he came of age, when he would return to take command.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The reply approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The petition was approved.

sentences.zh: 鞏未至京卒，朝弼遂得嗣。

translations.literal: Before Gong reached the capital he died, and Chaob then succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Gong died before reaching the capital, and Chaob thus succeeded.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十年，元江土舍那鑒叛。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Jiajing the native adjutant Na Jian of Yuanjiang rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of the Jiajing reign, Na Jian, a native adjutant of Yuanjiang, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 詔朝弼與都御史石簡討之，分五軍薄其城。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chaob and Censor-in-Chief Shi Jian to campaign against him; five armies were divided to press against the city.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Chaob and Censor-in-Chief Shi Jian to suppress the rebellion; they divided five armies and closed in on the city.

sentences.zh: 城垂拔，以瘴發引還。

translations.literal: The city was nearly taken, but miasma broke out and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The city was nearly taken, but when pestilence broke out they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔罷簡，將再出師。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed Jian and was about to send out the army again.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dismissed Shi Jian and prepared to launch another campaign.

sentences.zh: 鑒懼仰藥死，乃已。

translations.literal: Jian in fear took poison and died, and then it ended.
translations.idiomatic: Na Jian, terrified, took poison and died, and the campaign was called off.

sentences.zh: 四十四年討擒叛蠻阿方李向陽。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he campaigned against and captured the rebel tribesman Afang Li at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year he captured the rebel chieftain Afang Li at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，平武定叛酋鳳繼祖，破賊巢三十餘。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he pacified Wuding, defeating the rebel chieftain Feng Jizu and destroying more than thirty rebel strongholds.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign he pacified Wuding, defeating the rebel chieftain Feng Jizu and destroying more than thirty rebel lairs.

sentences.zh: 朝弼素驕，事母嫂不如禮，奪兄田宅，匿罪人蔣旭等，用調兵火符遣人詗京師。

translations.literal: Chaob had always been arrogant; he did not serve his mother and sister-in-law according to propriety, seized his elder brother's fields and dwellings, harbored criminals such as Jiang Xu, and using military tallies for mobilization sent men to spy on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chaob had long been arrogant; he failed to treat his mother and sister-in-law with proper respect, seized his elder brother's lands and property, harbored criminals such as Jiang Xu, and used military tallies to mobilize troops and send agents to reconnoiter the capital.

sentences.zh: 乃罷朝弼，以其子昌祚嗣，給半祿。

translations.literal: Chaob was then dismissed; his son Changzuo succeeded with half stipend granted.
translations.idiomatic: Chaob was dismissed, and his son Changzuo succeeded him with half stipend.

sentences.zh: 朝弼怏怏，益放縱。

translations.literal: Chaob was resentful and became all the more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Chaob grew resentful and became increasingly unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 葬母至南京，都御史請留之。

translations.literal: When burying his mother he reached Nanjing; the Censor-in-Chief requested that he be detained.
translations.idiomatic: While taking his mother for burial he reached Nanjing, and the censor-in-chief petitioned to detain him.

sentences.zh: 詔許還滇，毋得預滇事。

translations.literal: An edict permitted him to return to Yunnan but forbade involvement in Yunnan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed him to return to Yunnan but forbade him from meddling in Yunnan matters.

sentences.zh: 朝弼恚，欲殺昌祚。

translations.literal: Chaob was enraged and wished to kill Changzuo.
translations.idiomatic: Chaob was enraged and plotted to kill Changzuo.

sentences.zh: 撫按交章言狀，併發其殺人通番諸不法事，逮系詔獄論死。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator and regional inspector submitted successive memorials describing the situation, also exposing his killings, trafficking with foreigners, and other unlawful acts; he was arrested, imprisoned in the imperial prison, and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coordinator and regional inspector memorialized in succession, also exposing his murders, illegal trade with foreigners, and other crimes; he was arrested, held in the imperial prison, and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 援功，錮之南京，卒。

translations.literal: His meritorious service was invoked; he was confined in Nanjing until death.
translations.idiomatic: On account of his past service his sentence was commuted; he was confined in Nanjing, where he died.

sentences.zh: 昌祚初以都督僉事總兵官鎮守，久之嗣公爵。

translations.literal: Changzuo at first served as regional commander and commander-in-chief as Assistant Chief Controller; after a long time he succeeded to the ducal title.
translations.idiomatic: Changzuo initially served as assistant chief controller and regional commander-in-chief; only after many years did he succeed to the dukedom.

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年，姚安蠻羅思等叛，殺郡守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli the tribesmen of Yao'an, Luo Si and others, rebelled and killed the prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Wanli reign, Luo Si and other tribesmen of Yao'an rebelled and killed the prefect.

sentences.zh: 昌祚與都御史鄒應龍發土、漢兵討之，破向寧、鮓摩等十餘寨，犁其巢，盡得思等。

translations.literal: Changzuo with Censor-in-Chief Zou Yinglong mobilized native and Han troops to campaign against them, broke more than ten stockades including Xiangning and Zamó, uprooted their lairs, and captured Si and the rest entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Changzuo and Censor-in-Chief Zou Yinglong raised native and Han troops against them, stormed more than ten stockades including Xiangning and Zamó, uprooted their strongholds, and captured Luo Si and his followers.

sentences.zh: 十一年，隴川賊嶽鳳叛附緬甸，挾其兵侵旁近土司。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the bandit Yue Feng of Longchuan rebelled and attached himself to Burma, using its troops to invade neighboring native offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the bandit Yue Feng of Longchuan rebelled, threw in his lot with Burma, and used Burmese troops to raid neighboring native jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 昌祚壁洱海，督裨將鄧子龍、劉綎等斬木邦叛酋罕虔，以暑瘴退師。

translations.literal: Changzuo fortified at Erhai Lake and directed lieutenant generals Deng Zilong, Liu Ting, and others to behead Han Qian, rebel chieftain of Mong Mao; they withdrew the army on account of summer miasma.
translations.idiomatic: Changzuo encamped at Erhai Lake and directed lieutenant generals Deng Zilong, Liu Ting, and others to execute Han Qian, the rebel chieftain of Mong Mao; they then withdrew on account of the summer pestilence.

sentences.zh: 明年復攻罕虔故巢，三道併入，擒其酋罕招等，又破緬兵於猛臉。

translations.literal: The next year they again attacked Han Qian's former lair; three columns entered together, captured chieftains including Han Zhao, and again defeated Burmese troops at Menglian.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they struck at Han Qian's former stronghold again; three columns advanced together, captured chieftains including Han Zhao, and routed Burmese forces at Menglian.

sentences.zh: 嶽鳳降。

translations.literal: Yue Feng surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Feng submitted.

sentences.zh: 論功加太子太保，悉食故祿。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted his full former stipend.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to grand guardian of the heir apparent and restored to his full former stipend.

sentences.zh: 復以次平羅雄諸叛蠻，再賜銀幣。

translations.literal: He again in sequence pacified various rebel tribes of Luoxiong and was once more granted silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to pacify the rebel tribes of Luoxiong in turn and was again rewarded with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 緬兵攻猛廣，昌祚會師壁永昌，緬人遁，追擊至那莫江，瘴作而還。

translations.literal: Burmese troops attacked Mengguang; Changzuo assembled his forces and fortified at Yongchang; the Burmese fled; pursuit reached the Namo River, miasma arose, and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Burmese troops attacked Mengguang, Changzuo assembled his forces and encamped at Yongchang; the Burmese fled, and though he pursued them to the Namo River, pestilence forced his withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，緬人復入寇，昌祚逐之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the Burmese again invaded; Changzuo drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the Burmese invaded again, and Changzuo drove them back.

sentences.zh: 連戰俱捷，遂傅於緬，會群蠻內亂乃還。

translations.literal: Successive battles were all victorious; they then pressed close to Burma, but when various tribes fell into internal disorder they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Battle after battle went his way, and his army pressed deep into Burma, but when the tribes erupted in internal disorder he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 沐氏在滇久，威權日盛，尊重擬親王。

translations.literal: The Mu clan had long been in Yunnan; their power and authority grew daily, and the esteem shown them rivaled that of imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: The Mu clan had long held sway in Yunnan; their power grew by the day, and the honors paid them rivaled those accorded imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 昌祚出，僉事楊寅秋不避道，昌祚笞其輿人。

translations.literal: When Changzuo went out, Assistant Controller Yang Yinqiu did not yield the road; Changzuo had his sedan bearers flogged.
translations.idiomatic: When Changzuo went abroad, Assistant Controller Yang Yinqiu failed to clear the way; Changzuo had his sedan bearers beaten.

sentences.zh: 寅秋訴於朝，下詔切責。

translations.literal: Yinqiu complained to the court, and an edict was issued with stern rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: Yinqiu appealed to the court, and an edict sharply rebuked Changzuo.

sentences.zh: 已，以病，命子叡代鎮。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on account of illness, his son Rui was ordered to hold command in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, taken ill, he was ordered to have his son Rui hold command in his stead.

sentences.zh: 武定土酋阿克叛，攻會城，脅府印去。

translations.literal: The native chieftain Ake of Wuding rebelled, attacked the provincial seat, and seized the prefectural seal and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Ake, the native chieftain of Wuding, rebelled, attacked the provincial capital, and carried off the prefectural seal.

sentences.zh: 叡被逮下獄，昌祚復理鎮事。

translations.literal: Rui was arrested and imprisoned; Changzuo again took charge of command affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was arrested and thrown into prison, and Changzuo resumed command.

sentences.zh: 卒，孫啟元嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his grandson Qiyuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his grandson Qiyuan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 卒，子天波嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son Tianbo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Tianbo succeeded.

sentences.zh: 十餘年而土司沙定洲作亂，天波奔永昌。

translations.literal: After more than ten years the native official Sha Dingzhou raised a rebellion; Tianbo fled to Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a decade the native official Sha Dingzhou rebelled, and Tianbo fled to Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 亂定，復歸於滇。

translations.literal: When the disorder was settled he returned again to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was put down he returned to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 永明王由榔入滇，天波任職如故。

translations.literal: When Prince Yongming Youlang entered Yunnan, Tianbo served in office as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yongming Zhu Youlang entered Yunnan, Tianbo continued in office as before.

sentences.zh: 已，從奔緬甸。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed him in flight to Burma.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he followed the prince in flight to Burma.

sentences.zh: 緬人欲劫之，不屈死。

translations.literal: The Burmese wished to coerce him; he would not submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Burmese sought to coerce him, he refused to yield and died.

sentences.zh: 初，沙定洲之亂，天波母陳氏、妻焦氏自焚死。

translations.literal: At the beginning, during Sha Dingzhou's rebellion, Tianbo's mother Lady Chen and his wife Lady Jiao burned themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: At the outbreak of Sha Dingzhou's rebellion, Tianbo's mother, Lady Chen, and his wife, Lady Jiao, burned themselves to death.

sentences.zh: 後天波奔緬，妾夏氏不及從，自縊死。

translations.literal: Later when Tianbo fled to Burma, concubine Lady Xia could not follow in time and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Tianbo fled to Burma, his concubine Lady Xia was unable to follow in time and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 逾數十日收葬，支體不壞，人以為節義所感焉。

translations.literal: After several tens of days her body was retrieved for burial; her limbs were not decayed, and people considered it a marvel wrought by her chastity and fidelity.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten days later her body was retrieved for burial; her flesh had not decayed, and people took it as a marvel wrought by her faithfulness and virtue.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：明興諸將，以六王為稱首。

translations.literal: The Commentator says: At the founding of Ming, among the generals the Six Princes stood foremost.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentator says: At the rise of the Ming, among all its generals the Six Princes stood foremost.

sentences.zh: 非獨功茂，亦由其忠誠有以契主知焉。

translations.literal: It was not only that their achievements were abundant; it was also because their loyalty matched the sovereign's trust.
translations.idiomatic: It was not merely that their achievements were great; their loyalty also won the sovereign's deepest trust.

sentences.zh: 親莫如岐陽，舊莫如東甌，而寧河、黔甯皆以英年膺腹心之寄。

translations.literal: None was closer in kinship than Qiyang, none more ancient in companionship than Dong'ou, while Ninghe and Qianning both in their prime received the charge of the sovereign's innermost trust.
translations.idiomatic: None was closer in kin than Qiyang, none more venerable in long service than Dong'ou, while Ninghe and Qianning, still in their prime, were entrusted with the sovereign's most intimate confidence.

sentences.zh: 汗馬宣勞，純勤不二，旂常炳耀，洵無愧矣。

translations.literal: Sweating horses they proclaimed their toil; pure and diligent without wavering; banners and bells shine bright—in truth without shame.
translations.idiomatic: They toiled on horseback and proclaimed their labors, pure and steadfast to the end; their banners and bells blaze forth in glory—they were truly beyond reproach.

sentences.zh: 岐陽敦詩說禮，以儒雅見重，東甌乞身歸第，以明哲自全，皆卓然非人所能及。

translations.literal: Qiyang cultivated poetry and expounded ritual, esteemed for scholarly refinement; Dong'ou begged leave to retire to his estate, preserving himself through wise discernment—these were all outstanding and beyond what others could reach.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyang cultivated the classics and was honored for scholarly grace; Dong'ou begged leave to retire home and preserved himself through wise withdrawal—each in his way was extraordinary, beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 獨黔寧威震遐荒，剖符弈世，勳名與明相始終。

translations.literal: Only Qianning's might shook the distant wilds; enfeoffed with tally across generations, his fame endured with Ming from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Qianning alone made his might felt across the far frontiers; enfeoffed with imperial tally from generation to generation, his renown endured with the dynasty from its founding to its fall.

sentences.zh: 而寧河盡瘁馳驅，功高齡促，後嗣亦少所表見。

translations.literal: Yet Ninghe exhausted himself in rushing about; his achievements were lofty but his years brief, and his descendants showed little distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Ninghe, by contrast, wore himself out in constant campaigns—great were his deeds, but brief his life, and his descendants distinguished themselves little.

sentences.zh: 論者謂諸王之遺澤，隆替有殊，然而中山有增壽，與岐陽之有景隆，追溯先烈，不無遺憾。

translations.literal: Commentators say the legacy left by the princes rose and fell in unequal measure; yet Zhongshan had Zengshou, even as Qiyang had Jinglong—looking back at the founding worthies, there is no little regret.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators observe that the blessings the princes left behind waxed and waned unequally; yet Zhongshan had Zengshou even as Qiyang had Jinglong—looking back at the founding heroes, one must feel regret.

sentences.zh: 榮遇之弗齊，亦安見其有幸有不幸哉。

translations.literal: That their honors received were not equal—how then can one say some were fortunate and some unfortunate?
translations.idiomatic: Since their rewards were unequal, who is to say which were favored and which were not?
